Recommend the two to three most effective formats per pillar (long article, short video, infographic, newsletter, webinar, podcast, etc.). 5. Define a primary and a secondary success metric per pillar. 6. Design the recommended production distribution per pillar (% of monthly total). OUTPUT: Content-pillar document with: pillar summary table + detailed card per pillar + recommended production distribution + criteria for adding or retiring a pillar in the future. EDGE CASES: If the brand operates across multiple segments, design sub-pillars per segment within the main pillars. If the competition already dominates a thematic territory, redirect that pillar toward a differentiating angle. If the team is small (fewer than two people), limit to three pillars to maintain consistency. [C · CRITERIA] Each pillar has a distinct identity from the others, a clear intent, and enough sub-topics for at least six months of production. Trade-off: breadth of pillars (more potential traffic) vs. concentration (more thematic authority). DoD: minimum three complete pillars with a detailed card, eight sub-topics each, and defined metrics. Protocolo MetodologIA: pillars must derive from the brand's value proposition, not from generic sector trends.
spec-marketing_repurposing_contenido_ato: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team invests significant time and budget producing long-form content (articles, webinars, podcasts, reports) that is published only once on its original channel and then goes undistributed. The absence of a repurposing system means that content produces a single initial impact when it could multiply into dozens of derived pieces for multiple channels, audiences, and formats. [P · REQUEST] Design a repurposing and atomization system for the provided long-form content, generating the complete map of derived pieces, the exact formats per channel, and the workflow so that the team can replicate the system consistently with any future content. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a content distribution strategist specializing in repurposing and atomization, with experience designing systems that multiply the reach of a single piece of content into fifteen or more formats distributed efficiently across five or more channels. ASSUMPTIONS: The team has access to basic editing tools (Canva, CapCut or equivalent, text editor); the default channels are blog, LinkedIn, Instagram, newsletter, and YouTube Shorts or TikTok; the source content is in Spanish. If the content is not provided, design the system with a generic example from the inferred sector. INPUTS: Paste the source content (article, webinar transcript, report summary) below. STEPS: 1. Identify the five to eight key messages or ideas from the source content. 2. Map each key idea to the most appropriate formats and channels (blog post, LinkedIn thread, Instagram carousel, video clip, newsletter, infographic, quote card, X thread, podcast episode, etc.). 3. Generate the text or script for the three to five highest-impact pieces as examples for immediate production. 4. Design the reusable workflow: roles, tools, estimated times, checklist per format. 5. Calculate the impact multiplier: total pieces generated, channels covered, estimated potential reach. OUTPUT: Atomization map (idea × format × channel table) + texts or scripts for the three to five priority pieces + reusable workflow + production checklist per format. EDGE CASES: If the source content is very short, limit to three to four formats maximum and recommend enriching the base content first. If the team is one person, simplify the workflow to the two highest-ROI channels. If the content has legal or confidentiality restrictions, indicate which sections not to atomize. [C · CRITERIA] The atomization map covers at least four distinct channels with at least ten derived pieces. Each derived piece has a format, channel, example text or script, and estimated production time. DoD: replicable system with checklist + minimum three pieces ready to publish. Trade-off: volume of pieces (more reach, more effort) vs. depth per channel (fewer pieces, higher quality). Protocolo MetodologIA: prioritize the derived pieces that generate the greatest incremental reach in the channels with the brand's most active audience.
spec-marketing_briefing_pieza_contenido: [S · SITUATION] A content team needs to commission the production of a specific piece (article, video, infographic, podcast, newsletter) from a copywriter, designer, or producer. Without a detailed and standardized brief, the piece is delivered outside the strategic objective, with the wrong tone, without the necessary keywords, or in the wrong format for the channel, generating rework and delays. [P · REQUEST] Generate a complete production brief ready to deliver to the person responsible for the piece, containing all the elements needed for the professional to execute without additional meetings. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a content director with experience standardizing editorial processes and writing briefs that minimize rework in creative teams. ASSUMPTIONS: The brief is for a digital piece in Spanish; the production professional has a professional level but does not know the company's strategic context; the piece must be published within the next 15 days. If the piece type or channel is not specified, ask only that before continuing. INPUTS: Paste the piece name, publication channel, objective, and any additional relevant information (keyword, audience, style references, restrictions) below. STEPS: 1. Identify the piece type, channel, objective, and audience from the provided inputs. 2. Structure the brief with all standard sections. 3. Complete each section with specific and actionable information (not generic). 4. Include at least two style or format reference examples of the expected tone. 5. Define the observable acceptance criteria the editor will use to approve the piece. OUTPUT: Complete brief with sections: executive summary, business and content objective, target audience and funnel stage, target keyword and secondary keywords (if applicable for blog/SEO), suggested structure with H1/H2/H3 hierarchy, tone and voice with examples, style references, technical specifications (length, file format, resolution if applicable), delivery deadline and publication date, acceptance criteria, contact for questions. EDGE CASES: If the piece is a video, replace the keywords section with a suggested opening script. If it is an infographic, include a diagram of the information flow. If there are brand or legal restrictions, document them explicitly. If the client has no style references, the content director proposes three from the sector. [C · CRITERIA] The brief can be executed by an external professional without a clarification meeting. Each section contains specific, non-generic information. DoD: complete brief with observable acceptance criteria. Trade-off: brevity of the brief (less writing time, greater misinterpretation risk) vs. exhaustiveness (more rework prevented). Protocolo MetodologIA: the brief is a delivery contract; every field left empty or generic is a documented rework risk.
spec-marketing_guion_video_corto_hook: [S · SITUATION] A content creator or marketing team needs to produce short videos (15 to 90 seconds) for vertical-scroll platforms (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) that maximize viewer retention in the first three seconds and sustain attention through the final call to action. Most videos fail because the hook is weak, the pace drops halfway through, or the close generates no action. [P · REQUEST] Write a complete short-video script with a hook-retention-close structure, optimized for the indicated platform, the supplied topic, and the target duration, ready to record without further adjustments. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a scriptwriter specialized in short-form video for social platforms, with experience writing scripts that achieve retention rates above 60% in branded videos for B2B and B2C sectors. ASSUMPTIONS: The video is in Latin American Spanish; the default duration is 60 seconds (approximately 150 spoken words); the default platform is Instagram Reels or TikTok; the default goal is brand awareness or education. If the topic is unclear, ask only for the topic and the audience before proceeding. INPUTS: Paste the video topic, platform, target duration, goal (education, entertainment, conversion), and any constraints (specific CTA, product to mention) below. STEPS: 1. Identify the most powerful hook for the topic (question, striking statistic, controversial claim, identification situation). 2. Structure the video in three acts: hook (0–3 sec), development (3–80% of duration), close with CTA (last 15–20%). 3. Write the complete script with voiceover cues (pause, emphasis, speed) and basic visual notes (on-screen text, shot change). 4. Generate three hook variants for A/B testing. 5. Propose the publication caption text and three high-performance hashtags for the platform. OUTPUT: Full script with voiceover cues and visual notes + three hook variants for A/B testing + caption + hashtags. EDGE CASES: If the topic is complex, prioritize a single central idea and leave the rest for other videos in the series. If the video is from a regulated sector (health, finance), include the appropriate disclaimer in the script without interrupting the narrative flow. If the platform is LinkedIn, shift the tone to more professional and extend to 60–90 seconds. [C · CRITERIA] The hook can be recorded alone (without context) and generate curiosity in a cold viewer. The pace does not exceed four words per second. The CTA is one single specific action. DoD: complete script ready to record + three hook variants. Trade-off: hook originality (more memorable, more writing time) vs. proven template (less risk, less differentiation). Protocolo MetodologIA: the script is optimized first for retention at three seconds and second for conversion; not a single second of the video may be expendable.
spec-marketing_storytelling_marca_viaje_: [S · SITUATION] A brand or company needs to build a powerful brand narrative that connects emotionally with its audience, differentiates its value proposition from competitors, and is consistently applicable across all communication channels. The brand exists but its messages are functional and rational; there is no story that generates identification, preference, and loyalty. [P · REQUEST] Design the complete brand narrative using the Hero's Journey framework, where the customer is the hero and the brand is the guide or mentor, resulting in a master story that can be adapted to all formats and communication channels. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a senior brand strategist and scriptwriter with experience building brand narratives for technology, professional services, and mass-consumer companies, using storytelling frameworks (Campbell's Hero's Journey, Donald Miller's StoryBrand structure) to generate emotional connection and competitive differentiation. ASSUMPTIONS: The brand has identified its target customer and differential value proposition; if not provided, they will be inferred from the sector and declared as an assumption; the customer is the hero of the story (not the brand); the brand acts as an expert guide. If the sector has specific cultural sensitivities in Latin America, consider them in the narrative. INPUTS: Paste the brand description, value proposition, target customer profile, main problems it solves, and main competitors below. STEPS: 1. Define the hero profile (customer): who they are, what they want, what prevents them from achieving it (external and internal obstacle). 2. Position the brand as the guide: what credibility it has, what empathy it demonstrates, what plan it delivers. 3. Build the complete narrative arc: the customer's ordinary world, the call to adventure, obstacles, meeting the guide, transformation plan, success, and new identity. 4. Extract the key messages from the narrative in three formats: brand tagline (5–7 words), positioning paragraph (50 words), full story (300–500 words). 5. Design the narrative applications for four channels: home page (headline + subheadline + CTA structure), LinkedIn (opening post), elevator pitch (30 seconds), and welcome email. OUTPUT: Applied Hero's Journey framework + tagline + positioning paragraph + master story (300–500 words) + four channel applications. EDGE CASES: If the brand has multiple customer segments, build a master narrative and adaptation notes per segment. If the company is B2B with long sales cycles, shift the tone to business transformation narrative rather than personal transformation. If the brand is new and has no real success stories, use the aspiration archetype with [ASSUMPTION] marked. [C · CRITERIA] The customer is the protagonist throughout the entire narrative (the brand is never the hero). The customer's internal obstacle is explicitly named. The promised transformation is specific and observable. DoD: complete master narrative + four channel applications ready to use. Trade-off: narrative specificity (more powerful, less flexible) vs. genericity (more reusable, less memorable). Protocolo MetodologIA: the customer is always the hero; if the brand appears as protagonist in any sentence the narrative fails its purpose; the promised transformation must be specific and observable.
spec-marketing_contenido_storybrand_sb7: [S · SITUATION] A brand wants to restructure the central message of its website, landing page, or content piece so the customer is the hero and the brand is the guide, following the 7 blocks of the StoryBrand framework (character, problem, guide, plan, call to action, success, avoidable failure). [P · REQUEST] Produce a brand message document with the 7 SB7 blocks fully written, ready to use as the copywriting foundation for the home page, hero section, and welcome emails. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior content strategist specialized in StoryBrand and conversion copywriting. ASSUMPTIONS: if no product/service is provided, infer B2B SaaS; if no audience is provided, assume a decision maker at a mid-sized company; proceed declaring assumptions if confidence ≥ 0.85, otherwise ask a maximum of 3 things. INPUTS: product/service description and audience pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the character and their external, internal, and philosophical desire → 3-row table. 2. Formulate the problem at 3 levels (external, internal, philosophical) with an implicit villain. 3. Position the brand as the guide with empathy and authority in 2–3 sentences. 4. Design a plan of 3 clear, actionable steps. 5. Write a direct CTA and a transition CTA. 6. Paint the success picture in 3–5 concrete points. 7. Describe the avoidable failure with urgency without being manipulative. OUTPUT: structured document with each block titled, text ready to copy, and a suggested usage note per block. EDGE CASES: (a) brand with multiple audiences → prioritize the one with the highest lifetime value and annotate variations; (b) highly technical product → simplify language to the decision-maker level, add inline glossary; (c) brand with no clear differentiator → frame the guide around the unique process, not the product. [C · CRITERIA] Each block must pass the 5-second reading test; the customer must appear as the active subject in ≥ 80% of sentences; the CTA must be a specific imperative verb; DoD: 7 complete blocks, coherent with each other, without unexplained technical jargon. Protocolo MetodologIA: apply StoryBrand SB7 with audience evidence before drafting any block.
spec-marketing_topical_authority_hub: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team wants to position itself as an authority on a specific topic in search engines and networks, but its current content is scattered and without hierarchy. It needs a content hub with a pillar page, cluster articles, and an internal linking network that consolidates topical authority with Google and the audience. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a complete content hub architecture: 1 pillar page with section structure, 8–12 cluster articles with title, search intent, and subtopics, and an internal linking map. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior SEO strategist specialized in topical authority and content architecture. ASSUMPTIONS: if no central topic is provided, assume the sector of the mentioned business; if there is no keyword data, generate semantically plausible titles declaring it; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: central topic and business description pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the umbrella topic and first- and second-level subtopics → semantic tree. 2. Design the pillar page: H1, 6–8 H2 sections with content description and target keyword. 3. Propose 8–12 cluster articles: SEO title, search intent (informational/commercial/transactional), subtopics to cover, primary keyword. 4. Design the internal linking network: which cluster points to the pillar and what cross-links exist between clusters. 5. Estimate publication frequency to cover the hub in 90 days. OUTPUT: pillar page table, cluster articles table (columns: title, intent, keyword, subtopics), internal linking network in hierarchical list format, 90-day plan. EDGE CASES: (a) highly technical niche with low search volume → prioritize semantic authority over volume, add technical-depth content; (b) multi-product brand → create one hub per product line, do not mix; (c) blog from scratch → start with 4 clusters of highest commercial intent before expanding. [C · CRITERIA] Each cluster article must cover a distinct subtopic without cannibalizing the pillar; the linking network must be bidirectional in ≥ 70% of pairs; the 90-day plan must be executable with 2 writers; DoD: semantic tree + cluster table + linking map + 90-day calendar. Protocolo MetodologIA: validate the semantic coherence of the tree before proposing individual titles.
spec-marketing_serie_newsletter_editoria: [S · SITUATION] A brand or content creator wants to launch or restructure their newsletter with a defined editorial line that maintains thematic consistency, publication rhythm, and voice, so that subscribers know exactly what to expect and when. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete design of an editorial series for a newsletter: series name, frequency, structure of each edition, fixed sections, topics for the first 8 editions, and an editorial voice guide. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior editorial director with experience in high-engagement newsletters for professional audiences. ASSUMPTIONS: if no niche is specified, assume digital marketing for entrepreneurs; if no frequency, propose weekly; proceed declaring assumptions if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: niche, audience, and newsletter goal pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the editorial concept: series name, tagline, and unique value proposition in 2 sentences. 2. Design the fixed structure of each edition: 4–6 sections with name, estimated length, and purpose. 3. Establish the frequency and send day/time with brief justification. 4. Create the calendar of the first 8 topics: tentative title, editorial angle, special section for the edition. 5. Draft the voice guide: 5 tone traits + 5 words/phrases NEVER used + 2 sentence examples. OUTPUT: document with editorial concept, edition structure, calendar of 8 topics, and voice guide — all ready to hand off to the writing team. EDGE CASES: (a) very broad audience → segment the concept to one primary archetype and annotate future variations; (b) existing newsletter → preserve existing name/frequency and reformulate sections; (c) solo creator → simplify structure to 3 sections maximum for sustainability. [C · CRITERIA] The value proposition must differentiate itself from the 3 most popular newsletters in the niche; each fixed section must have a memorable name; the 8 topics must cover the variety of the niche without repeating; DoD: concept + structure + calendar + voice guide completed. Protocolo MetodologIA: differentiate the editorial concept from the generic niche before proposing sections or topics.
spec-marketing_contenido_skyscraper_mejo: [S · SITUATION] A content team has a URL or existing content piece that fails to rank above competitors in organic search, and wants to apply the Skyscraper technique: analyze what is already ranking, identify its gaps, and produce a notably superior version. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a Skyscraper improvement plan: gap analysis of the reference content, a new outperforming structure, a list of concrete improvements, and a publication checklist. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior SEO On-Page specialist and content editor with proven experience in the Skyscraper technique. ASSUMPTIONS: if no reference content is provided, assume the top-1 organic URL will be pasted; if no target keyword, infer it from the article title; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85 declaring the assumption. INPUTS: existing proprietary content and/or competitor reference URL pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Analyze the reference content: identify topics covered, depth, formats used, implicit backlinks from authority signals → comparative table. 2. Identify 5–8 content gaps: uncovered topics, unanswered questions, outdated data, missing formats. 3. Propose a new outperforming H1/H2/H3 structure with a description of each section and its advantage vs. the reference. 4. List concrete improvements: add statistical data, insert comparison table, add FAQs, include diagram, improve meta title and description. 5. Generate a 10-point publication checklist: technical SEO + content + distribution. OUTPUT: comparative table, prioritized gap list, full structure with descriptions, improvement list, and publication checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) very long reference content (>3,000 words) → segment the analysis by thematic blocks; (b) highly competitive topic with high DR → focus on long-tail angle and technical depth; (c) no access to competitor content → work with the titles visible in the SERP and declare the limitation. [C · CRITERIA] The new structure must cover ≥ 3 identified gaps; the improved content must be at least 30% more complete in subtopics; the checklist must include at least 3 technical SEO points; DoD: analysis + structure + improvements + checklist completed. Protocolo MetodologIA: back each gap with a reference to the analyzed content before proposing improvements.
spec-marketing_modelo_contenido_tofu_mof: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team wants to ensure its content strategy covers all stages of the conversion funnel: cold audience attraction (TOFU), prospect nurturing (MOFU), and sales closing (BOFU), avoiding the bias of producing content for only one stage. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a complete content map with at least 5 pieces per stage (TOFU/MOFU/BOFU), format type, conversion goal, distribution channel, and measurement KPI for each piece. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior content and sales funnel strategist with experience in B2B/B2C inbound marketing. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business is specified, assume B2B SaaS with a 30–90-day sales cycle; if no buyer persona, assume a marketing manager at a mid-sized company; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: business description, product, and buyer persona pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the buyer journey: awareness, consideration, and decision stages with pain points per stage. 2. Map 5 TOFU pieces: high organic-distribution formats (blog, video, infographic, reel, podcast) with specific topic and traffic goal. 3. Map 5 MOFU pieces: capture and nurturing formats (lead magnet, webinar, case study, comparison, email sequence) with topic and qualified-lead conversion goal. 4. Map 5 BOFU pieces: closing formats (demo, free trial, testimonial, ROI calculator, personalized proposal) with topic and sale or meeting goal. 5. Assign distribution channel and primary KPI per piece → unified table. OUTPUT: table of 15 pieces with columns (stage, title, format, goal, channel, KPI), 3-stage buyer journey, and prioritization note by impact vs. effort. EDGE CASES: (a) low-ticket business with short cycle → reduce MOFU and strengthen BOFU with urgency; (b) new brand without audience → prioritize 3 high-volume TOFU pieces before investing in MOFU; (c) small team → prioritize reusable formats (one webinar → 5 clips + article). [C · CRITERIA] Each piece must have a measurable KPI; the map must cover the 3 stages in 40/35/25 proportions (TOFU/MOFU/BOFU); DoD: table of 15 pieces + buyer journey + prioritization note. Protocolo MetodologIA: align each piece to the stage pain point before assigning format or channel.
spec-marketing_guia_estilo_editorial: [S · SITUATION] A brand or content team produces articles, posts, and emails with inconsistent voice, tone, and format because no reference document exists to standardize how to write. The absence of a guide generates editorial rework and loss of brand identity in every published piece. [P · REQUEST] Produce a complete, operational editorial style guide that the writing team can use from day one, without depending on the editor's subjective criteria. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior content director with experience in brand voice and style editing for digital brands. ASSUMPTIONS: if no brand information is provided, assume a B2B technology brand with a professional yet approachable tone; if no content examples, work with the audience brief; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: brand name, audience description, 2–3 existing content examples, or voice brief pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the editorial personality: 4–5 voice adjectives + opposites to avoid. 2. Establish tone rules by format: blog, email, social media, landing page. 3. Draft structure standards: paragraph length, use of lists, headings, bold, and quotation marks. 4. Specify inclusive language, technical jargon, and brand term rules. 5. Create a list of 10 forbidden words or phrases with their recommended alternative. 6. Include 3 before/after editing examples applying the guide. OUTPUT: document of 4–6 titled sections, ready to hand off to any external writer, with concrete examples in each rule. EDGE CASES: (a) brand with multiple product lines with distinct tones → define the umbrella voice and annotate variations per line; (b) multilingual team → specify whether rules apply only to Spanish or are adapted; (c) brand with long history → review the 5 most successful content pieces to extract real patterns before writing the guide. [C · CRITERIA] Each rule must be applicable without ambiguity by a junior writer; the before/after examples must show a perceptible difference; the guide must not exceed 4 pages of quick reading; DoD: 6 complete sections with concrete examples. Protocolo MetodologIA: extract real patterns from existing content before codifying any style rule.
spec-marketing_estructura_campana_paid_s: [S · SITUATION] An advertiser wants to launch or restructure their paid search campaigns (Google Ads or Microsoft Ads) by segmenting on search intent to maximize ad relevance, Quality Score, and return on ad spend. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete paid search campaign architecture segmented by intent: campaign and ad group structure, bidding logic by intent, match types, and suggested negatives. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior paid search specialist with experience in Google Ads and high-performance account architectures. ASSUMPTIONS: if no product or conversion goal is provided, assume lead generation for SaaS; if no budget, propose a scalable structure without mentioning amounts; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: product/service, conversion goal, and target audience pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Classify relevant search intents into 3–4 categories: informational, comparative, transactional, brand. 2. Design the campaign architecture: campaign name, goal, predominant match type, and destination landing page per campaign. 3. Propose 3–5 ad groups per campaign with example thematic keywords. 4. Recommend a bidding strategy per campaign type (Target CPA, Maximize Conversions, Manual CPC) with justification. 5. List 15–20 essential negative keywords to avoid irrelevant traffic. OUTPUT: campaign architecture tree (hierarchical text), ad group table with example keywords, bidding strategy table per campaign, negatives list. EDGE CASES: (a) very limited budget → consolidate into 2 priority campaigns (transactional + brand) and defer the rest; (b) local business → add geographic modifiers and location extensions; (c) product with high SKU variety → use Performance Max campaign type as a complement, not replacement. [C · CRITERIA] Each ad group must have thematic keyword coherence; negatives must cover the 3 most common types of irrelevant traffic in the niche; the bidding strategy must be aligned with the declared conversion goal; DoD: tree + AdGroup table + bidding table + negatives list. Protocolo MetodologIA: segment by real search intent before assigning campaigns or ad groups.
spec-marketing_estructura_meta_ads_cbo: [S · SITUATION] An advertiser wants to structure their Meta Ads campaigns (Facebook and Instagram) using campaign-level budget optimization (CBO) to distribute spend efficiently across ad sets with differentiated audiences, maximizing conversions at the lowest possible cost. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete Meta Ads CBO campaign architecture: campaign structure, ad sets with segmentation, recommended creative types per set, and budget and bidding configuration. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior media buyer specialized in Meta Ads with experience in CBO strategies and account scaling. ASSUMPTIONS: if no conversion goal is provided, assume purchases or leads; if no audience data, propose standard cold/warm/hot segmentation; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: product/service, goal, indicative daily budget, and available audiences pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the campaign structure by goal: prospecting (cold audience), retargeting (warm), and conversion (hot) in separate campaigns with CBO in each. 2. Design 2–4 ad sets per campaign with distinct segmentation criteria (interests, lookalike, behaviors, URL retargeting). 3. Recommend creative types per set: static image, carousel, short video, UGC — with message angle description. 4. Specify CBO configuration: minimum spend threshold per set (if applicable), bidding strategy (Lowest Cost or Cost Cap), and scaling logic. 5. List basic automation rules to pause low-performing sets. OUTPUT: hierarchical campaign tree, ad set table with segmentation and recommended creative, CBO configuration table, and automation rules. EDGE CASES: (a) low budget (<50 USD/day) → consolidate into 1 CBO campaign with maximum 3 ad sets; (b) pixel without enough data → use traffic or engagement objective first to feed the pixel; (c) product catalog → add a Dynamic Ads campaign as a fourth campaign. [C · CRITERIA] Each ad set must have a non-overlapping audience with the others; the bidding strategy must be justified by the expected conversion volume; automation rules must be actionable from day one; DoD: tree + ad set table + CBO table + automation rules. Protocolo MetodologIA: separate cold, warm, and hot audiences into distinct campaigns before assigning creatives or bids.
spec-marketing_copy_anuncio_search_rsa: [S · SITUATION] An advertiser needs to create responsive search ads (RSA) for Google Ads that leverage the format's flexibility: up to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions that the algorithm combines optimally. The challenge is to write variations distinct enough for Google to have useful combinations, yet coherent with the keyword and the value proposition. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a complete RSA set ready to upload: 15 headlines (max. 30 characters each), 4 descriptions (max. 90 characters each), with variations covering different message angles (benefit, urgency, differentiator, CTA, question). [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior paid search copywriter with experience in Google Ads RSA and ad-relevance Quality Score optimization. ASSUMPTIONS: if no target keyword is provided, infer it from the described product/service; if there is no landing page, assume the proposition matches the copy; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: product/service, target keyword, unique value proposition, and desired CTA pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the 5 key message angles: main benefit, competitive differentiator, urgency/scarcity, social proof, and direct CTA. 2. Write 15 headlines distributed across the 5 angles (3 headlines per angle), respecting the 30-character limit. 3. Write 4 descriptions of up to 90 characters each, each developing a different angle with a CTA. 4. Verify that at least 3 headlines include the target keyword or a semantic variation. 5. Review that no headline duplicates the concept of another. OUTPUT: table with 15 numbered headlines + the angle they belong to + character count; table with 4 descriptions + angle + character count. EDGE CASES: (a) very long keyword → use the short version in headlines and the full version in descriptions; (b) highly technical product → simplify the benefit to the customer outcome in the headlines; (c) brand with legal restrictions → avoid superlatives and guarantees in headlines, use them in descriptions with nuance. [C · CRITERIA] No headline may exceed 30 characters; no description may exceed 90 characters; ≥ 3 headlines must include the keyword or a semantic synonym; all 5 angles must be represented; DoD: 15 headlines + 4 descriptions in a table with verified character counts. Protocolo MetodologIA: cover all 5 message angles before verifying character limits.
spec-marketing_creativos_paid_social_ang: [S · SITUATION] A performance marketing team needs to scale its paid social campaigns (Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn) but has run out of fresh ideas for creatives. Audience fatigue from repeating the same message angle is increasing CPM and lowering CTR. The solution is to systematize creative production using a matrix of distinct angles for the same product. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a paid social creative matrix with 6–8 distinct message angles, each with concept, headline copy, visual/video description, first-3-second hook, and recommended format. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior creative strategist specialized in paid social with experience in Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, and LinkedIn Ads. ASSUMPTIONS: if no platform is specified, design for Meta Ads (feed and stories); if there is no customer avatar, infer from the product; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: product/service, target audience, value proposition, and platform pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the 6–8 most effective message angles for the product: problem/pain, aspiration/transformation, social proof, objection/myth, urgency, education, comparison, identity. 2. For each angle: write the concept in 1–2 sentences, the text headline/hook, the visual or video description (what is seen, what is heard), the first-3-second hook, and the recommended format (static image, carousel, 15-second video, 60-second video, UGC). 3. Add the recommended CTA per angle. 4. Indicate the audience temperature level each angle works best for (cold, warm, hot). OUTPUT: matrix table with columns (angle, concept, headline/hook, visual description, 3-second hook, format, CTA, temperature). EDGE CASES: (a) highly visual product → prioritize 4 video angles; (b) B2B product → adapt social proof and education angles, reduce urgency; (c) low production budget → mark creatives that can be produced with a smartphone and UGC. [C · CRITERIA] No angle may repeat the same central concept; the 3-second hooks must differ in structure (question, statement, data point, shock); each angle must indicate audience temperature; DoD: 6–8 angles in a complete table with all fields. Protocolo MetodologIA: differentiate the angles by psychological mechanism before drafting any copy.
spec-marketing_estructura_audiencias_pai: [S · SITUATION] A paid social advertiser wants to build an audience architecture segmented by temperature (cold: never interacted with the brand; warm: interacted but not converted; hot: already customers or have shown direct intent) to personalize the message and conversion objective at each funnel level. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete audience architecture by temperature for Meta Ads or the indicated platform: definition of each segment, inclusion/exclusion criteria, estimated size, and recommended message per segment. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior media buyer specialized in paid social audience architecture and conversion funnel strategy. ASSUMPTIONS: if no platform is specified, design for Meta Ads; if no pixel is installed, propose interest-based audiences as cold and manual segmentation as warm; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: product/service, ads platform, current available audiences (custom audiences, lookalikes, pixel) pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define cold audiences: 3–4 broad interest or behavior segments, 1% lookalike, and 3–5% lookalike with justification. 2. Define warm audiences: website visitors (last 30/60/90 days), content engagers (video views, page engagement), landing page visitors without conversion. 3. Define hot audiences: past buyers, active customers, payment page visitors, customer email list. 4. Establish cross-exclusion logic: hot excluded from cold and warm, warm excluded from cold. 5. Recommend the campaign objective and creative type appropriate for each temperature. OUTPUT: audience table with columns (temperature, segment name, inclusion criteria, exclusion criteria, estimated size [ASSUMPTION if no real data], recommended campaign objective, creative type). EDGE CASES: (a) account with no pixel or data → use only cold interest audiences and defer warm/hot; (b) large customer base → create high-intent lookalike from best customers (top 25% by LTV); (c) high-frequency repurchase product → create an inactive customer segment (no purchase in 90+ days) as a special warm segment. [C · CRITERIA] Cross-exclusions must be specified without overlap; estimated sizes must be marked [ASSUMPTION] if there is no real data; the campaign objective must be aligned to the temperature; DoD: complete table with all three temperature levels, exclusions, and recommendations. Protocolo MetodologIA: define cross-exclusions before assigning campaign objectives or creatives to each segment.
spec-marketing_estrategia_pujas_objetivo: [S · SITUATION] A paid media advertiser has active campaigns on Google Ads and/or Meta Ads but is unclear about which bidding strategy to use for each objective (reach, traffic, leads, sales, retention), resulting in budget waste or inconsistent results because the bidding strategy is not aligned to the business objective or the available conversion volume. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a bidding strategy decision map: for each campaign objective, the recommended bidding strategy, its conditions of use, its risks, and the daily control metric. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior paid media specialist with experience in advanced bidding strategies on Google Ads and Meta Ads for accounts of varying sizes and pixel maturity. ASSUMPTIONS: if no platform is specified, cover both Google Ads and Meta Ads in separate tables; if there is no conversion data, recommend manual strategies as a starting point; proceed if confidence ≥ 0.85. INPUTS: platform(s), active or planned objectives, approximate monthly conversion volume, and target CPA or ROAS pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. List the relevant campaign objectives: reach/awareness, traffic, lead generation, sales (ecommerce), retention/upsell. 2. For each objective: identify the most appropriate bidding strategy in Google Ads (Manual CPC, Enhanced CPC, Target CPA, Target ROAS, Maximize Conversions, Maximize Conversion Value) and in Meta Ads (Lowest Cost, Cost Cap, Bid Cap, Minimum ROAS, Value Optimization). 3. Specify conditions of use: minimum required conversion volume, required pixel maturity, recommended minimum daily budget. 4. Flag the risks of each strategy and the signals that indicate it is failing. 5. Recommend the daily control metric and the alert threshold for manual intervention. OUTPUT: Google Ads table (objective, strategy, conditions, risks, control metric), Meta Ads table with the same fields, and a decision guide as a 4–5 node question tree. EDGE CASES: (a) new account with no history → start with Manual CPC / Lowest Cost and migrate to automated upon reaching 30–50 conversions/month; (b) very aggressive ROAS target → use Target ROAS with a 20% buffer above the real figure to avoid volume restriction; (c) branding campaigns without direct conversion → use CPM or Reach objective with frequency cap. [C · CRITERIA] Each strategy must have quantifiable conditions of use; risks must include at least one detectable signal in the metrics; the decision tree must reach a concrete recommendation in ≤ 5 questions; DoD: Google Ads table + Meta Ads table + decision tree. Protocolo MetodologIA: align the bidding strategy to available conversion volume before recommending automation.
spec-marketing_secuencia_retargeting_pai: [S · SITUATION] An ecommerce or digital service brand has active paid media campaigns (Meta Ads, Google Ads, or TikTok Ads) and has segmented audiences by behavior: product page visitors, checkout initiators, and past buyers. Direct conversion rates are low and the team needs a structured retargeting sequence by intent level to recover users at different funnel stages. [P · REQUEST] Design a complete retargeting sequence of 3 to 5 levels ordered by intent heat, specifying audience, message, ad format, maximum frequency, time window, and exclusion rule for each level; delivered as a table + implementation narrative. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior performance marketing specialist with over 7 years designing retargeting funnels on Meta Ads and Google Ads for ecommerce brands with average ticket between 50 and 500 USD. ASSUMPTIONS: primary platform Meta Ads unless the user indicates otherwise; physical product with checkout on own site; pixel or tag installed and firing correctly; attribution window 7-day click / 1-day view; no sensitive category restrictions [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: site URL or product description pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify and name the available audience segments based on pixel-tracked behavior. 2. Order the segments from highest to lowest intent temperature and assign a level (L1 hottest → L5 coldest). 3. For each level: define the exact audience, main message (hook + value proposition + CTA), recommended format, maximum weekly frequency, active time window, and mandatory exclusion rule. 4. Draft at least one copy example for levels L1 and L2. 5. Generate a summary table and platform configuration notes. OUTPUT: 5-column table (Level, Audience, Key Message, Format/Frequency/Window, Exclusions) + copy example section + technical implementation notes; 600–900 words. EDGE CASES: (a) retargeting audience fewer than 1,000 users → extend the time window or combine segments noting this; (b) single-purchase product (non-recurring) → exclude buyers from all acquisition campaigns and adjust L5 to lookalike prospecting; (c) total retargeting budget under 500 USD/month → collapse to 3 levels and concentrate 60% on L1–L2. [C · CRITERIA] Each level has an audience mutually exclusive from higher levels; messages escalate in urgency as the intent level decreases; the table is self-executable without prior brand knowledge; no conversion metrics are invented without marking [ASSUMPTION]. DoD: complete table with 5 columns, at least 3 defined levels, 2 copy examples, and implementation notes delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before writing a single level, declare the platform and available audience assumptions so the user can correct them.
spec-marketing_plan_pruebas_creativas_pa: [S · SITUATION] A performance marketing team manages paid media campaigns and needs to systematize the production and evaluation of creatives to stop making decisions based on intuition. They currently launch ads without a defined testing framework, resulting in inconsistent outcomes and wasted budget on creatives that are never properly validated. [P · REQUEST] Produce an iterative creative testing plan including: structure of variables to test, minimum sample size per variant, victory criteria, iteration cycle (weeks), and a results tracking template; delivered as an actionable guide ready to implement this week. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Creative testing strategist with experience in controlled experiment methodology applied to paid media on Meta Ads, TikTok Ads, and Google UAC, accustomed to managing testing budgets between 500 and 10,000 USD/month. ASSUMPTIONS: Meta Ads platform; campaign objective conversions; testing budget of 15–20% of total paid media budget; minimum 50 conversions per variant to declare a winner; 2-week test round horizon [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: product description, conversion objective, and total monthly budget pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify and prioritize the creative variables to test (format, hook, value proposition, CTA, dominant emotion) using an impact vs. ease matrix. 2. Design the structure of the first test round: number of variants, budget per variant, and duration. 3. Define the primary metric and secondary evaluation metrics. 4. Establish victory criteria (minimum statistical significance or practical business rule). 5. Describe the iterative cycle: how the winning variant becomes the new control for the next round. 6. Deliver a tracking template in table format (Round, Variant, Variable tested, Investment, Result, Decision). OUTPUT: 3-section guide (Test structure, Victory criteria, Iterative cycle) + tracking template ready to copy; 500–800 words total. EDGE CASES: (a) total budget under 1,000 USD/month → reduce to 2 variants per round and extend to 3-week cycles; (b) account history under 6 months → prioritize format and hook tests before value proposition; (c) seasonal product with short window → compress cycle to 1 week with a 30-conversion threshold, noting the loss of statistical confidence. [C · CRITERIA] The plan specifies the exact number of variants, budget per variant, and duration for the first round; victory criteria are observable without complex manual calculation; the template can be used directly in a spreadsheet. DoD: 3-section guide delivered, tracking template included, explicit victory criteria. Protocolo MetodologIA: before designing the first round, declare the variable being tested and why it has the greatest leverage.
spec-marketing_calculo_target_roas_break: [S · SITUATION] An ecommerce or digital service business invests in paid media campaigns and needs to know the minimum ROAS (break-even) it must achieve to not lose money, and the target ROAS that justifies scaling spend. The marketing team makes bidding and budget decisions without a numerical reference anchored to the business economics, leading to over-investment or cutting profitable campaigns prematurely. [P · REQUEST] Calculate the break-even ROAS and target ROAS with a target profit margin from the business financial data; deliver the formulas, step-by-step calculation, and a sensitivity table with at least 3 margin scenarios. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Marketing analyst specializing in unit economics and financial modeling applied to paid media, with experience evaluating ecommerce campaigns with average tickets between 30 and 1,000 USD. ASSUMPTIONS: variable costs include COGS, payment gateway fee (3%), and logistics/shipping cost; fixed costs are not assigned per order but to the overall marketing budget; target gross margin of 30% of revenue if the user does not specify [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: average selling price, product cost (COGS), shipping cost, platform commissions, and any additional variable cost pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Calculate the unit gross margin: net revenue after variable costs per order. 2. Calculate break-even ROAS: 1 / (unit gross margin / selling price). 3. Calculate target ROAS for different target profit margins (10%, 20%, 30%). 4. Build a sensitivity table showing how the target ROAS changes when COGS varies ±10% and ±20%. 5. Translate the target ROAS to maximum CPA for the campaign. 6. Add an interpretive note: what each figure means for bidding decisions. OUTPUT: commented formulas section + calculation with user's data + sensitivity table (3 margin scenarios × 3 COGS scenarios) + bidding decision interpretation; 400–600 words. EDGE CASES: (a) multi-SKU bundle product → use weighted AOV and note it; (b) service with no tangible COGS → use cost of service delivery as a substitute; (c) channel with variable platform commission → use the range and present a conservative and optimistic scenario. [C · CRITERIA] Formulas are reproducible manually; the sensitivity table covers at least 9 combinations; the interpretation connects each ROAS to a concrete bidding action (raise, hold, lower); no margins are invented without marking [ASSUMPTION]. DoD: formulas, calculation with user data, sensitivity table, and bidding decision note delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before calculating, list the cost items to be included and confirm no relevant variable cost is missing.
spec-marketing_estructura_pmax_assets: [S · SITUATION] A Google Ads advertiser wants to launch or restructure a Performance Max (PMax) campaign and needs to organize the asset groups correctly to maximize the relevance of Google's machine learning. Poor asset grouping leads Google to serve irrelevant combinations of headlines, images, and audiences, wasting budget and reducing effective Quality Score. [P · REQUEST] Design the asset group structure for a PMax campaign: recommended number of groups, segmentation criterion per group, list of required assets by type (headlines, descriptions, images, videos, final URLs, audience signals), and a pre-launch quality checklist; delivered as a ready-to-use configuration guide for Google Ads. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Certified Google Ads specialist focused on Performance Max campaigns for ecommerce and lead generation, with experience configuring more than 50 PMax campaigns since 2022. ASSUMPTIONS: Google Ads account with conversions correctly configured; initial segmentation by product line or user intent; audience signals based on customer lists and website visitors; minimum budget of 50 USD/day per asset group [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: business description, main products or services, and conversion objective pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the asset group segmentation criterion (by product, by intent, by geography, or by retargeting vs. prospecting audience). 2. Recommend the initial number of asset groups and their names. 3. For each asset group, list the required assets with technical specifications (image dimensions, video duration, character limits). 4. Define the recommended audience signals per group. 5. Build a pre-launch quality checklist (minimum ad strength: Good; minimum video assets; final URLs with UTM parameters). OUTPUT: asset group structure table + asset technical specifications + 10-to-15-item pre-launch checklist; 500–750 words. EDGE CASES: (a) fewer than 1,000 conversions in the last 30 days → launch with 1 single asset group to accelerate the learning phase; (b) no proprietary video → indicate that Google will auto-generate videos and recommend uploading at least one high-quality landscape image to avoid low-quality videos; (c) catalog of more than 100 SKUs → recommend a connected product feed instead of manual URLs. [C · CRITERIA] The structure is executable directly in Google Ads without additional setup; the checklist includes at least 10 verifiable items; asset technical specifications are exact per current Google standards. DoD: structure table, technical specifications, and 10+ item checklist delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before designing the asset groups, declare the chosen segmentation criterion and justify why it is the most appropriate for the business objective.
spec-marketing_plan_medios_paid_mix: [S · SITUATION] A digital business or consumer brand has a monthly paid media budget and needs to decide how to distribute it among available channels (Meta Ads, Google Search, Google Shopping, TikTok Ads, YouTube, LinkedIn, etc.) to reach its awareness, traffic, or conversion objectives efficiently. The lack of a structured media plan results in excessive concentration on one channel, under-representation of key audiences, and no criteria for reallocating budget based on performance. [P · REQUEST] Create a monthly paid media plan with budget allocation by channel: justification for channel selection, percentage and amount assigned to each, primary objective and KPI per channel, and a budget reallocation rule if a channel does not meet its KPI; delivered as a media plan table + strategy narrative. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior media planner with experience in paid mix strategy for B2C and B2B brands with budgets between 5,000 and 100,000 USD/month, accustomed to optimizing the channel mix based on the customer journey. ASSUMPTIONS: primary objective conversions (sales or leads); B2C adult audience aged 25–45 unless the user indicates otherwise; short purchase cycle (less than 7 days) [ASSUMPTION]; no category restrictions. INPUTS: total monthly budget, primary objective (sales, leads, awareness), product/service description, and geographic market pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Map the customer journey in 3 stages (awareness, consideration, conversion) and assign channels to each stage. 2. Select 3 to 5 primary channels with justification based on audience reach, format, and journey stage. 3. Assign budget percentage to each channel with USD amount. 4. Define the primary KPI and minimum performance threshold per channel. 5. Establish a budget reallocation rule: if a channel's KPI falls below threshold for 2 consecutive weeks, redistribute X% to the best-performing channel. 6. Include a monthly review note. OUTPUT: media plan table (Channel, Journey stage, % budget, Monthly USD, Primary KPI, Minimum threshold) + 200–300 word strategic narrative + explicit reallocation rule; total 600–900 words. EDGE CASES: (a) budget under 3,000 USD/month → concentrate on 2 direct conversion channels and defer awareness; (b) geographic market under 500,000 people → reduce to 2 channels and adjust expected CPMs; (c) B2B product with long purchase cycle → increase proportion of budget on nurturing sequences, reduce Meta. [C · CRITERIA] The allocation sums to 100% of budget; each channel has explicit KPI and threshold; the reallocation rule is actionable without ambiguity; the channel selection justification connects each channel to the customer journey. DoD: complete table, strategic narrative, and reallocation rule delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the plan, declare the assumed customer journey and primary objective so the user can correct them.
spec-marketing_diagnostico_fatiga_creati: [S · SITUATION] A performance marketing team notices that its paid media campaigns show signs of deterioration in engagement and cost metrics: CTR drops week over week, CPM rises, and CPA worsens without changes to the bid or the audience. The probable cause is creative fatigue, but the team lacks a framework to confirm it or a creative rotation plan to prevent it systematically. [P · REQUEST] Conduct the creative fatigue diagnosis from campaign metrics and design a creative rotation plan that includes: alert threshold, rotation calendar, retirement criteria, and minimum new asset production per cycle; delivered as a diagnostic report + actionable rotation plan. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Creative strategy and performance marketing specialist with experience diagnosing creative fatigue in Meta Ads and TikTok Ads accounts managing more than 20 active creatives simultaneously. ASSUMPTIONS: Meta Ads platform; available metrics: CTR, CPM, frequency, CPA, and link click rate; fatigue alert threshold: frequency greater than 3 in 7 days OR CTR with a 20% week-over-week drop for 2 consecutive weeks [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: metrics from the last 4 weeks per creative (CTR, CPM, frequency, CPA, impressions) pasted in the thread; alternatively, a qualitative description of observed behavior. STEPS: 1. Evaluate each creative against the defined alert thresholds to confirm or rule out fatigue. 2. Classify creatives into three statuses: active with no signals, on alert, and retiring. 3. Propose the rotation calendar: frequency of introducing new creatives, minimum number of fresh assets per 2-week cycle, and grace window for new creatives before evaluating them. 4. Define the retirement process: when a creative moves from on-alert to retiring and whether it can be reactivated after a rest period. 5. Production recommendations: types of new creatives to produce based on current winners. OUTPUT: creative status table (Creative, CTR weeks 1–4, CPM, Frequency, Status, Action) + rotation calendar + retirement and reactivation rules; 500–700 words. EDGE CASES: (a) fewer than 5 active creatives → the diagnosis covers all of them and the rotation plan must ensure at least 8 in rotation; (b) no data broken down by creative → diagnose at ad set level using aggregated trends and note the limitation; (c) account with production budget restrictions → prioritize copy variants over new audiovisual formats. [C · CRITERIA] The diagnosis classifies each creative in one of the three defined statuses; the rotation plan specifies concrete dates or frequencies; production recommendations are actionable with the team's resources. DoD: status table, rotation calendar, and retirement rules delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the diagnosis, declare the alert thresholds to be used so the user can calibrate them to their context.
spec-marketing_secuencia_email_bienvenid: [S · SITUATION] A digital or ecommerce brand has just implemented a subscription or registration form and needs to convert new subscribers into buyers or active users through a welcome email sequence. Without a structured sequence, new contacts arrive at the moment of highest interest and engagement, but the brand fails to capitalize on that window to generate the first conversion or establish the relationship. [P · REQUEST] Write a sequence of 5 to 7 welcome and onboarding emails including: subject line, preview text, email body (structured in sections), main CTA, and send timing from opt-in; delivered as a draft ready to load into the ESP. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Copywriter specializing in email marketing and onboarding sequences for ecommerce and SaaS brands, with a track record of sequences achieving open rates above 40% in the first 72 hours. ASSUMPTIONS: generic ESP (Klaviyo or Mailchimp); segment: new subscribers who have not yet purchased; warm and conversational tone unless the user specifies otherwise; email 1 is sent immediately after opt-in; emails 2–5 are sent on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: brand name, main value proposition, 3 key product/service benefits, welcome offer (if any), and brand tone pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Design the sequence narrative arc: what objective each email fulfills (welcome + promise, education, social proof, objection, urgency, follow-up). 2. Write each email with subject line, preview text, personalizable greeting, body of 3 to 5 paragraphs, and a clear CTA. 3. Indicate the send timing in hours or days from opt-in. 4. Mark personalization fields with [NAME], [PRODUCT], etc. 5. Add a recommended A/B testing note for the subject line of email 1. OUTPUT: 5 complete emails (subject line, preview text, body, CTA, timing) ready to copy into the ESP; body length 150–300 words per email. EDGE CASES: (a) Brand with no welcome offer → replace the discount incentive with exclusive value content (guide, checklist, video). (b) Subscriber who purchases before email 4 → indicate that the ESP should remove the contact from the sequence when the purchase is recorded. (c) B2B brand or high-ticket product → extend the sequence to 10 emails and increase the weight of educational content over direct offer. [C · CRITERIA] Each email has a unique subject line under 50 characters, differentiated preview text, a single CTA, and explicit timing; the sequence has narrative progression without repeating the same message; personalization fields are uniformly marked. DoD: 5 complete emails with all required fields delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before writing, present the sequence narrative arc (one objective per email) for approval before developing the copy.
spec-marketing_flujo_carrito_abandonado: [S · SITUATION] An ecommerce store loses between 60% and 80% of carts before the customer completes the purchase. The marketing team knows that abandoners are the highest-purchase-intent segment on the site, but lacks a structured recovery flow combining emails and, optionally, SMS to reconvert them into buyers in the first 24–72 hours after abandonment. [P · REQUEST] Design a 3-email (and optionally 1 SMS) abandoned cart recovery flow with: exact timing from abandonment, subject line, preview text, body, CTA, and flow exit logic when a purchase is detected; delivered as a technical specification ready to implement in the ESP. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Email marketing and ecommerce automation specialist with experience implementing cart recovery flows in Klaviyo and Shopify that recover between 5% and 15% of abandoned carts. ASSUMPTIONS: ESP platform Klaviyo integrated with Shopify; flow triggers when the "Checkout Started" event is not followed by "Order Placed" within 1 hour; the subscriber has a registered email; the flow uses dynamic product personalization (image, name, price) [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: brand name, average cart value, available recovery offer (discount, free shipping, or other), and brand tone pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the flow activation logic and exit condition (purchase detected = exit). 2. Write email 1 (mild urgency, no discount): timing 1 hour after abandonment, reminder with product image. 3. Write email 2 (social proof + objection): timing 24 hours, include reviews or guarantee. 4. Write email 3 (incentive + last chance): timing 72 hours, include recovery offer. 5. (Optional) Design a 1-line SMS for timing 4 hours if email 1 was not opened. 6. Specify the flow exit logic when a purchase is detected between emails. OUTPUT: flow specification with text logic diagram + 3 complete emails (subject line, preview text, body, CTA) + 1 optional SMS + Klaviyo configuration notes; total length 500–750 words. EDGE CASES: (a) No recovery offer available → email 3 emphasizes stock scarcity and return guarantee instead of discount. (b) Average cart value under 30 USD → simplify to 2 emails to avoid exhausting the audience. (c) Subscriber on suppressed list due to complaints → indicate that the ESP should automatically exclude them from the flow. [C · CRITERIA] The timing of each email is exact in hours; the flow exit logic is defined; email 1 does not offer a discount to protect margin; product personalization fields are marked with Klaviyo or generic syntax. DoD: flow logic, 3 complete emails, and configuration notes delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before writing, confirm the activation logic and flow exit condition to align with the ESP configuration.
spec-marketing_segmentacion_lista_rfm: [S · SITUATION] An ecommerce brand has a subscriber base with purchase history and sends the same emails to the entire list, resulting in declining open and click rates, frequent unsubscribes, and deliverability risk. The team needs to segment the list using the RFM model (Recency, Frequency, Monetary) to send differentiated messages to each segment and improve communication relevance. [P · REQUEST] Design the RFM segmentation of the email list: definition of scoring thresholds for each dimension (R, F, M), the resulting segments with name and description, the recommended communication strategy per segment, and the optimal send cadence; delivered as a segmentation guide ready to implement in the ESP. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: CRM and email marketing specialist with experience applying RFM models to ecommerce databases of 10,000 to 500,000 contacts to optimize segmentation and customer lifetime value. ASSUMPTIONS: RFM scoring scale of 1 to 5 per dimension; total score between 3 and 15; between 5 and 8 strategic segments defined; purchase data available in the ESP or exportable from the ecommerce platform [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: approximate list size, average purchase frequency, AOV, and ESP used pasted in the thread; alternatively, request that the model use B2C ecommerce reference values. STEPS: 1. Define scoring thresholds for Recency (days since last purchase), Frequency (number of purchases in the period), and Monetary (total accumulated value). 2. Assign scores from 1 to 5 for each dimension based on the thresholds. 3. Define the 5 to 8 strategic segments with name, combined score range, and customer profile description. 4. Design the communication strategy per segment: message type, offer, tone, and objective. 5. Establish the recommended send cadence per segment (emails per week). 6. Indicate how to implement the filters in Klaviyo or Mailchimp. OUTPUT: RFM threshold table + segment table (Name, Score, Profile, Strategy, Cadence) + ESP implementation notes; length 600–800 words. EDGE CASES: (a) Base with less than 6 months of history → use only Recency and Frequency (simplified RF model) and indicate this. (b) ESP without native purchase fields → indicate how to import external data as contact properties. (c) List with fewer than 500 buyers → do not apply full RFM; use email engagement segmentation instead. [C · CRITERIA] Thresholds are specific in days and quantities, not generic; each segment has a distinct strategy and cadence; the guide is implementable in Klaviyo or Mailchimp without advanced knowledge. DoD: threshold table, segment table, and implementation notes delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before defining the thresholds, declare the reference values you will use for R, F, and M so the user can adjust them to their business.
spec-marketing_lead_nurturing_drip: [S · SITUATION] A B2B or high-ticket services company has captured leads through a lead magnet or contact form. These leads are aware of the problem but are not ready to buy: they need education about the solution, trust building, and authority proof before moving to a sales conversation. The marketing team needs an educational drip sequence that progressively warms the lead until they are ready to be passed to sales or click on a conversion offer. [P · REQUEST] Design an educational drip sequence of 6 to 10 emails that takes the lead from the problem to the purchase decision: with a thematic arc per email, subject line, summarized body, CTA, and qualification signal (lead scoring trigger) to escalate the lead to sales; delivered as a sequence plan + draft emails. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Content and email marketing strategist specializing in B2B lead nurturing campaigns and mid-to-high-ticket services (1,000 to 50,000 USD), with experience designing sequences that shorten the sales cycle by 30–40% [ASSUMPTION]. ASSUMPTIONS: sales cycle of 30 to 90 days; send cadence: 1 email every 3 days; lead converted at the lead magnet and has not yet requested a demo or call; ESP with lead scoring (HubSpot, ActiveCampaign, or equivalent) [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: service or product description, main problem it solves, buyer persona profile (title, industry, main pain point), and final conversion offer (demo, call, trial) pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Design the sequence thematic arc: problem → aggravating factors → conceptual solution → differentiators → social proof → objections → decision. 2. Assign a topic and learning objective to each email. 3. Write subject line + preview text + summarized body (150–250 words per email) + soft or hard CTA depending on the stage. 4. Define 2 to 3 lead scoring signals (clicks on key CTA, pricing page visit, email reply) that escalate the lead to sales. 5. Indicate where in the sequence the sales conversation is proposed. OUTPUT: thematic arc table (Email N, Topic, Objective, CTA type) + 6 draft emails + lead scoring signals table; total length 700–1,000 words. EDGE CASES: (a) Sales cycle under 14 days → compress to 4 emails with higher density of social proof and a direct CTA from email 3. (b) Technical lead magnet (whitepaper, use case) → assume higher knowledge level and skip the basic education phase. (c) Product with no demo available → replace the demo CTA with a free consultation or case study access. [C · CRITERIA] The thematic arc has logical progression without jumps; each email has a single objective and a single CTA; the lead scoring signals are observable in the ESP without advanced configuration. DoD: thematic arc, 6 draft emails, and lead scoring signals delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before writing, present the complete thematic arc with one objective per email for review before developing the copy.
spec-marketing_subject_lines_ab_test: [S · SITUATION] An email marketing team is preparing a campaign or newsletter send and knows that the subject line is the factor with the greatest impact on open rate, but writes a single subject line without exploring alternatives or systematizing learning from previous tests. They need a process to generate multiple subject line variants based on different psychological levers, select the best candidates for an A/B test, and establish a replicable decision criterion. [P · REQUEST] Generate 10 to 15 subject line variants for a specific email using at least 5 distinct psychological levers, select the 2 best for the A/B test with justification, define the decision criterion (sample size, test duration, and decision metric), and leave a reusable template for future campaigns; all delivered as a working document ready for the team. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Email marketing copywriter with a specialty in consumer psychology and open rate optimization, with experience writing more than 500 tested subject lines in ESPs such as Klaviyo, Mailchimp, and HubSpot. ASSUMPTIONS: campaign objective is to maximize unique open rate; list of at least 5,000 subscribers for the A/B test to be statistically significant; test duration: 4 hours before sending to the rest of the list [ASSUMPTION]; spam words are not used (FREE in all caps, !!!). INPUTS: email topic, main offer or content, brand tone, and list segment pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Select the 2 best with justification. 5. Define the A/B test protocol: sample size per variant, duration, and decision metric (unique open rate). 6. Deliver tracking template: Campaign, Variant A, Variant B, Winner, Open Rate, Winning Lever. OUTPUT: list of 10–15 variants organized by lever + Top 2 selection with justification + A/B test protocol + reusable tracking template; total length 400–600 words. EDGE CASES: (a) List under 5,000 subscribers → indicate that the test will not reach statistical significance and recommend sending the variant with the best qualitative score. [C · CRITERIA] Variants cover at least 5 distinct levers; no variant exceeds 50 characters; the Top 2 selection is justified with lever + audience arguments; the test protocol specifies exact sample size and duration. DoD: 10–15 variants, justified Top 2, test protocol, and tracking template delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before generating the variants, declare the 5 levers that will be used and the evaluation criteria so the user can adjust them.
spec-marketing_reactivacion_winback_inac: [S · SITUATION] An ecommerce or SaaS brand has a growing percentage of inactive subscribers on its email list: contacts who have not opened or clicked any email in the last 90 to 180 days. spec-marketing_plan_deliverability_inbox:

spec-marketing_copy_email_ventas_pas:

spec-marketing_flujo_post_compra_cross_s:

spec-marketing_estrategia_organica_por_r:
