spec-marketing_serie_contenido_viral_hoo:
[S · SITUATION] A content creator or marketing team needs to produce a thematic series of social network publications that has narrative coherence, high retention, and viral potential, relying on proven hooks that capture attention in the first 3 seconds of reading or viewing. [P · REQUEST] Content series of a minimum of 7 publications on a given topic, with: series concept, narrative thread connecting the publications, unique hook for each publication (defined typology), guiding body copy, final CTA, and a bank of 20 reusable hooks classified by type. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior viral content strategist and copywriter with experience in organic growth on Spanish-speaking social networks. ASSUMPTIONS: main platform: LinkedIn or Instagram (whichever is specified; if not indicated, design for LinkedIn) [ASSUMPTION]; publication format: text with or without image [ASSUMPTION]; tone: expert-accessible unless otherwise specified [ASSUMPTION]; if no topic is specified, request it in the first declared assumption before proceeding. INPUTS: central topic of the series, platform, target audience, desired tone, series objective (awareness, leads, authority) (paste here). STEPS: 1. Define the concept and narrative axis of the series in 1 paragraph. 2. Design the architecture of 7 publications: title, hook type, and angle of each. 3. For each publication: write the opening hook, body structure, and specific CTA. 4. Ensure each publication works independently and also as part of the series. 5. Generate a bank of 20 reusable hooks classified by type (curiosity, controversy, statistic, promise, storytelling, disruptive question). 6. Include a per-platform adaptation note. OUTPUT: (a) Series concept in 1 paragraph; (b) Architecture table of 7 publications; (c) Full copy of each publication (hook + body + CTA); (d) Bank of 20 hooks classified by type; (e) Adaptation note for a variant on another network. EDGE CASES: (1) Very technical topic → use the first post to democratize the concept and generate curiosity, then go deeper; (2) Mixed audience (experts and beginners) → design alternating publications for each level; (3) Series for a launch campaign → integrate progressive revelation with anticipation between posts. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: series has 7+ complete publications with hook+body+CTA, bank of 20 classified hooks. Trade-off: virality vs. substance → attention-grabbing hooks but with bodies that fulfill the hook's promise. DoD: complete series with 7 publications, bank of 20 hooks, and adaptation note included.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that each publication has a differentiated hook, body that fulfills the promise, and a specific CTA, and that the bank includes 20 classified hooks before delivering.
spec-marketing_estrategia_short_form_vid:
[S · SITUATION] A brand or content creator wants to build presence and audience through short-form videos (15-90 seconds) published consistently on multiple platforms (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts). They currently have no documented strategy: they publish reactively, without a calendar or per-channel format criteria. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a complete multi-platform short-form video strategy: content pillars, recommended format per platform, weekly calendar, success metrics, and efficient production flow. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a senior digital content strategist specializing in short-form video and organic growth on social networks, with experience in B2C brands and independent creators. ASSUMPTIONS: if the user does not specify an industry or audience, assume a digital services brand targeting Spanish-speaking adults aged 25-40; if no production budget is specified, assume austere production with a smartphone and basic editing; proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste description of the business/brand, target audience, and priority platforms. STEPS: 1. Define 3-5 thematic pillars aligned to the business and audience interest. 2. Specify the optimal format per platform (duration, ratio, hooks, CTA). 3. Design a weekly calendar with frequency and content type per day. 4. Propose a batch production flow that allows recording 5 videos in one session. 5. Set tracking metrics at 30, 60, and 90 days. OUTPUT: structured document with a section per step; tables for calendar and metrics; production checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) brand in a regulated industry (finance, health) → add a legal review layer before publishing; (b) very niche audience with low search volume → prioritize collaborations and community hashtags over trends; (c) minimal production resources → simplify to a single reusable format on all platforms. [C · CRITERIA] Each pillar must be justified with at least one observable audience insight. The calendar must be sustainable without a dedicated team. DoD: the user can start recording the first video in less than 24 hours after reading the document.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that each pillar has an associated hook, format, and metric before delivering.
spec-marketing_kit_lanzamiento_social:
[S · SITUATION] A company or creator is less than 4 weeks from launching a new digital product, service, or event and needs to coordinate social network communication coherently. They do not have a documented launch kit: messages vary by channel, the team improvises, and key dates are not aligned. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a complete social launch kit: phased publication timeline (pre-launch, launch day, post-launch), copy adapted by platform, basic visual guidelines, and launch success metrics. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a digital marketing director specializing in product launches and awareness campaigns on social networks, with experience in startups and consumer brands. ASSUMPTIONS: if no specific product is indicated, assume a digital product (course, app, or software); if no audience is indicated, assume an existing community of 1,000-10,000 followers on networks; if no media budget is specified, assume 100% organic launch; proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste product/event name and description, launch date, active platforms, and main value proposition. STEPS: 1. Define the three launch phases with dates and objectives per phase. 2. Create at least 3 copies per platform (Instagram, LinkedIn, X/Twitter) for each phase. 3. Establish minimum visual guidelines: palette, communication typography, image/video formats. 4. Define a list of strategic hashtags and key mentions. 5. Set success metrics (reach, engagement, conversion) and decision milestones. OUTPUT: kit in table + text format per section; copy ready to copy and paste; pre-publication validation checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) launch in less than 7 days → compress phases and prioritize email over networks; (b) controversial or sensitive product → add a negative comment management protocol; (c) no prior audience → include a tactic for alliances with complementary accounts for amplification. [C · CRITERIA] Each copy must include a hook, value proposition, and explicit call to action. The timeline must not require more than 2 hours of daily team work. DoD: the team can publish the first kit content without any additional meeting.

Protocolo MetodologIA: confirm that the copy for each phase is distinguishable in tone before delivering the kit.
spec-marketing_mapeo_customer_journey:
[S · SITUATION] A marketing or product team needs to understand precisely how a customer experiences the buying journey from the moment they detect a need until they recommend the brand. No documented map exists: decisions about content, channels, and messaging are made without considering the customer's emotional state at each stage. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a complete customer journey map with stages, emotions, touchpoints, barriers, and intervention opportunities identified per phase; plus a prioritized action plan with the 3 highest-impact improvements. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a customer experience (CX) and behavioral marketing specialist with a strong foundation in consumer psychology and brand experience design. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business type is indicated, assume a B2C digital services business with a 1-4 week purchase cycle; if no real customer data is provided, work with industry-based archetypes and declare this; proceed with these assumptions without requesting further information. INPUTS: paste the business description, product or service, and any available customer data (reviews, surveys, frequent complaints). STEPS: 1. Define the journey stages: Awareness, Consideration, Decision, Purchase, Use, Loyalty, Referral. 2. For each stage: identify the dominant emotion, primary channel, key pain point, and brand opportunity. 3. Visualize the map in table format with columns per stage. 4. Identify the 3 highest-friction moments with root cause. 5. Propose an action plan with the 3 improvements prioritized by impact/effort. OUTPUT: complete journey table; 2-3 paragraph narrative describing the emotional arc; action plan with owner, metric, and estimated timeline. EDGE CASES: (a) business with multiple customer segments → create one map per priority segment; (b) impulse-purchase product (cycle < 24 hours) → compress stages to 3 and focus on Consideration and Decision; (c) business with high abandonment rate → prioritize barrier analysis in Decision and Purchase. [C · CRITERIA] Each stage must have at least one concrete, actionable intervention opportunity. The 3 action plan improvements must be launchable within 30 days. DoD: the team can use the map to make content and channel decisions without needing additional consulting.

Protocolo MetodologIA: validate that the emotional arc is coherent and progressive before delivering the map.
spec-marketing_modelo_funnel_tofu_mofu_b:
[S · SITUATION] A digital business needs to structure its marketing strategy into a coherent three-stage funnel: top of funnel (TOFU: generate awareness and traffic), middle of funnel (MOFU: nurture prospects and generate qualified leads), and bottom of funnel (BOFU: convert leads into customers). Currently the business creates content without distinguishing which funnel stage each piece addresses, resulting in inconsistent conversion. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete TOFU-MOFU-BOFU funnel design: objectives, content formats, channels, progression metrics, and transition flow between stages, with at least 3 concrete piece examples per stage. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a performance marketing consultant specializing in conversion funnel design for digital businesses and online education. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business type is indicated, assume an online education or consulting business with a ticket between 50 and 500 USD; if no primary channel is specified, assume a combination of organic content plus email marketing; proceed with these declared assumptions. INPUTS: paste the business description, main offer, target audience, and active channels. STEPS: 1. Define the objective and main metric for each stage (TOFU, MOFU, BOFU). 2. Propose 3-5 content formats per stage with a concrete topic example. 3. Specify the channel and transition mechanism from one stage to the next (lead magnet, email sequence, tripwire offer, etc.). 4. Define lead advancement criteria between stages. 5. Establish conversion metrics between stages (CTR, opt-in rate, purchase rate) and reference benchmarks. OUTPUT: funnel design table with columns per stage; list of concrete pieces; textual flow diagram; metrics table with benchmarks. EDGE CASES: (a) business with high ticket (>1,000 USD) → add a sales call stage between MOFU and BOFU; (b) cold audience with no prior community → extend TOFU duration and add a retargeting stage; (c) e-commerce business → adapt BOFU to abandoned cart and post-purchase upsell. [C · CRITERIA] Each stage must have a measurable objective, at least 3 content formats, and a clear transition mechanism to the next. DoD: the team can map any existing content piece within the funnel in under 5 minutes.

Protocolo MetodologIA: ensure that the transition mechanisms between stages are explicit and actionable before delivering.
spec-marketing_optimizacion_landing_conv:
[S · SITUATION] A business has an active landing page that receives traffic but converts below its industry benchmark. The team suspects issues in message hierarchy, CTA design, or value proposition, but lacks a structured analysis indicating what to change first. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a landing page conversion diagnosis with the 5 problems prioritized by impact, plus an optimization plan with specific changes, alternative copy where applicable, and A/B test criteria. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a conversion rate optimization (CRO) expert with experience auditing landing pages for digital products, SaaS, and consulting services. ASSUMPTIONS: if the URL or landing page content is not provided, work with the textual description the user provides; if the current conversion rate is not indicated, assume it is below 3% (a low benchmark for lead capture pages); proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste the complete landing page content (headline, subtitle, body, CTA, guarantees, testimonials, price if applicable) or the URL for analysis. STEPS: 1. Evaluate message hierarchy: headline, value proposition, benefits vs. features. 2. Analyze the CTA: position, copy, contrast, friction. 3. Review social proof: testimonials, numbers, logos. 4. Evaluate trust structure: guarantees, policies, security signals. 5. Identify the 5 main problems prioritized by estimated conversion impact. 6. Propose specific changes per problem: new copy, element repositioning, section additions/removals. 7. Design 2 A/B test hypotheses with a defined success metric. OUTPUT: diagnosis table with problem, severity, and estimated impact; proposed changes section with alternative copy; 2 A/B hypotheses in standard format. EDGE CASES: (a) landing with mixed cold/warm traffic → propose a differentiated variant by traffic source; (b) high-ticket product → add recommendation for a pre-sale page with a VSL video; (c) landing without testimonials → prioritize urgent collection of social proof before optimizing copy. [C · CRITERIA] Each proposed change must be implementable in under 2 hours without a developer. A/B hypotheses must have an estimated minimum sample size. DoD: the team can launch the first A/B test in under 48 hours.

Protocolo MetodologIA: order the 5 problems from highest to lowest estimated conversion impact before presenting the plan.
spec-marketing_diseno_lead_magnet_oferta:
[S · SITUATION] A digital business wants to grow its email list or community by capturing qualified leads, but its current capture offer (if one exists) is not attractive or specific enough for a new visitor to trade their email for it. It needs a lead magnet that solves a specific audience problem and acts as a first step toward the main offer. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete design of a high-converting lead magnet: concept, format, magnetic title, internal value-delivery structure, capture landing, and a 3-message welcome email sequence. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are an inbound marketing strategist and copywriter specializing in capture offer design and high-value list building in education, consulting, and digital product niches. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business type is indicated, assume an online education or consulting business; if the main audience problem is not specified, derive it from the business context and declare it as an assumption; if no desired format is indicated, recommend the one with the fastest production time that maintains high perceived value (e.g., checklist, template, or PDF mini-guide); proceed with declared assumptions. INPUTS: paste the business description, main paid offer, target audience, and the specific problem the business solves. STEPS: 1. Define the specific, urgent problem the lead magnet will solve (distinct from the main offer). 2. Select the optimal format with justification. 3. Create 3 title options using a specific-promise formula. 4. Design the lead magnet structure: table of contents or content flow in a maximum of 7 sections. 5. Write the capture landing copy: headline, subtitle, benefits list, and CTA. 6. Create a 3-email welcome sequence: lead magnet delivery, value activation, transition toward the main offer. OUTPUT: document with each section numbered; ready-to-implement copy; comparative table of the 3 titles with justification. EDGE CASES: (a) highly technical audience → prioritize a template or framework over educational content; (b) business without a defined main offer → design the lead magnet to also validate the problem to be solved; (c) existing but cold email list → adapt the lead magnet as a reactivation campaign. [C · CRITERIA] The lead magnet must be producible in under 4 hours. The delivery email must have a projected open rate above 40%. DoD: the business can have the capture active in under 48 hours.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that the lead magnet solves a specific problem distinct from the main offer before delivering the design.
spec-marketing_modelo_value_ladder:
[S · SITUATION] A digital business has one or two main offers but has not structured a value ladder that guides the customer from a free or low-cost entry point to a high-value offer. This limits customer lifetime value (LTV) and creates dependence on the constant acquisition of new customers to sustain revenue. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete design of a value ladder with 4-6 rungs: name, description, price, value promise, audience per rung, and ascension mechanism between levels; plus a prioritized implementation roadmap. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a digital business marketing strategist specializing in offer architecture and LTV maximization in education, consulting, and membership models. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business is indicated, assume consulting or online education in any professional niche; if no prices are specified, use representative ranges (free, 7-27 USD, 97-297 USD, 500-2,000 USD, 3,000-10,000 USD+); proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste the business description, existing offer(s) with prices, audience, and main transformation the business delivers. STEPS: 1. Map existing offers within the ladder. 2. Identify gaps (missing rungs) and propose offers for each. 3. Define per rung: commercial name, format, price, transformation promise, and customer profile that acquires it. 4. Design the ascension mechanism between each rung (CTA, upsell, call, continuity). 5. Prioritize the 2 next rungs to build using impact-on-LTV and ease-of-creation criteria. OUTPUT: ladder table with columns: Rung, Name, Format, Price, Promise, Ascension Mechanism; roadmap for the 2 next rungs with implementation steps. EDGE CASES: (a) business with a single high-ticket product → add a low-cost entry rung as a customer filter; (b) business with many products without a unifying thread → regroup into no more than 5 rungs with progressive transformation; (c) e-commerce business → adapt the ladder to physical products with complementary items and continuity. [C · CRITERIA] The ladder must have a logical transformation progression: each rung solves the next problem that emerges after completing the previous one. The ascension mechanism must be natural, not forced. DoD: the owner can explain the ladder to a prospect in under 2 minutes.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that the transformation progression between rungs is logical and non-overlapping before delivering.
spec-marketing_tripwire_oferta_entrada:
[S · SITUATION] A digital business has leads on its list or visitors on its site who have shown interest but have not yet purchased. It needs a very low-priced entry offer (tripwire) to convert prospects into first-time buyers, shifting their psychological relationship with the brand and opening the door to the main offer. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete design of a tripwire offer: concept, recommended price, bounded value promise, delivery format, short sales page copy, and a 3-message post-purchase follow-up sequence that leads toward the main offer. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a specialist in offer architecture and digital purchase psychology, with experience designing high-performing entry offers for education, consulting, and digital product businesses. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business is indicated, assume an online education or consulting business; if the main offer price is not specified, assume a ticket of 297-997 USD; the tripwire price should be between 1% and 5% of the main offer (typical range: 7-47 USD); proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste the business description, main offer, audience, and the most urgent specific problem of the ideal customer. STEPS: 1. Define the specific problem the tripwire will solve (a quick, visible result). 2. Select the most appropriate format (mini-course, premium template, recorded session, tool, etc.). 3. Recommend a price with psychological justification. 4. Write the short sales page copy: headline, promise, list of what is included, price with anchor, CTA, and low-risk guarantee. 5. Design a 3-email post-purchase follow-up sequence: delivery + quick win, result activation, bridge to the main offer. OUTPUT: concept and price section; ready-to-implement sales page copy; 3-email sequence with subject line and body. EDGE CASES: (a) very cold audience → add an intermediate context page before the tripwire; (b) very high-ticket main offer (>5,000 USD) → insert a mid-priced offer between the tripwire and the main offer; (c) list with no prior purchases → add artificial urgency (time-limited bonus) to the copy. [C · CRITERIA] The tripwire must be producible in under 8 hours. The tripwire promise must not be a degraded version of the main offer but a complementary result. DoD: the business can have the sales page active and the delivery email configured in under 24 hours.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that the tripwire promise generates a visible, fast result distinct from the main offer before delivering.
spec-marketing_modelo_lead_scoring:
[S · SITUATION] A digital business or sales team receives leads from multiple sources but has no objective criteria to prioritize which ones to contact first. The team spends similar time on cold and hot leads, reducing the efficiency of the sales process and the close rate. [P · REQUEST] Deliver an operational lead scoring model with two dimensions (fit to ideal profile + demonstrated level of interest), a scoring table by behavior and attribute, MQL/SQL classification criteria, and an action protocol by score segment. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a marketing and sales operations specialist (RevOps) with experience designing lead qualification systems for online education, SaaS, and B2B consulting businesses. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business type is indicated, assume a consulting or online education business with a 1-3 week sales cycle; if no CRM or tool is specified, assume the model will be implemented in a spreadsheet or basic CRM; proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste the business description, ideal customer profile (ICP) with demographic and firmographic attributes, and a list of observable lead behaviors (page visits, downloads, email opens, demo requests, etc.). STEPS: 1. Define ICP fit attributes with weight per attribute (summing to 100 points). 2. Define interest behaviors with score per behavior (with temporal decay if applicable). 3. Create the combined scoring table with ranges: Cold (0-39), Warm (40-69), Hot (70-89), SQL (90-100). 4. Define MQL and SQL criteria with score threshold and additional condition (if applicable). 5. Design the action protocol by segment: Cold → automated nurturing, Warm → targeted content, Hot → direct contact, SQL → handoff to sales. OUTPUT: attribute table with weights; behavior table with points; classification table by ranges; action protocol in decision-tree format. EDGE CASES: (a) business with low lead volume (<50/month) → simplify to a maximum of 5 attributes and 5 behaviors; (b) leads from multiple countries with very different profiles → create differentiated scoring by market; (c) no CRM → create a Google Sheets template with automated scoring formulas. [C · CRITERIA] The model must be applicable manually in under 3 minutes per lead. SQL criteria must be objective and verifiable without the seller's subjective judgment. DoD: the team can qualify the next incoming lead using the model without additional training.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that the MQL and SQL criteria are objective, binary, and verifiable before delivering the model.
spec-marketing_optimizacion_checkout_fri:
[S · SITUATION] A digital business or e-commerce store has a cart or checkout abandonment rate above its industry benchmark (above 70% for e-commerce, 60% for digital products). Customers reach the payment page with purchase intent but do not complete the transaction, generating a direct revenue loss on already-spent acquisition budget. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a diagnosis of friction points in the checkout process, an optimization plan with changes prioritized by impact and implementation difficulty, and alternative copy for the key payment page elements. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a digital purchase experience optimization specialist (checkout UX and CRO) with experience auditing payment flows on online education, SaaS, and e-commerce platforms. ASSUMPTIONS: if the current checkout is not provided, work with the most common friction patterns for the indicated business type; if the abandonment rate is not indicated, assume 70-75%; if the payment platform is not specified, assume Stripe, Hotmart, or WooCommerce depending on context; proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste the checkout flow description (steps, requested fields, available payment methods, error messages, visible guarantees) or screenshots if available. STEPS: 1. Map the current checkout flow step by step and identify each friction point. 2. Classify the friction by type: technical, psychological, design, trust. 3. Prioritize the 5 highest-friction points by estimated abandonment impact. 4. Propose specific changes per friction point with alternative copy where applicable. 5. Recommend trust elements to add: guarantees, security seals, urgency testimonials. 6. Propose a 3-message abandoned cart recovery sequence (email or SMS). OUTPUT: diagnosis table with friction type, severity, and estimated impact; optimization plan with prioritized changes; abandonment recovery sequence. EDGE CASES: (a) platform with no checkout customization options → focus on the pre-checkout page and the recovery sequence; (b) high-ticket product → add an installment payment option as a friction reduction lever; (c) international audience → review available payment methods by region. [C · CRITERIA] The highest-priority changes must be implementable without a developer in under 4 hours. The recovery sequence must be triggered within the first hour of abandonment. DoD: the business can implement the 3 highest-priority changes on the same day.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that each identified friction point has a concrete associated change before delivering the plan.
spec-marketing_webinar_funnel_evergreen:
[S · SITUATION] An online education or consulting business wants to generate sales in an automated way using a pre-recorded webinar that functions as an evergreen mechanism: the prospect registers, receives the on-demand webinar, and is guided toward a paid offer without manual team intervention. The business either does not have this system set up or has a version that does not convert well. [P · REQUEST] Deliver the complete design of the evergreen webinar funnel: registration page, pre-webinar email sequence, webinar structure with a script per section, post-webinar sales page, 5-email follow-up sequence, and funnel tracking metrics. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a marketing automation strategist specializing in evergreen webinar funnels and medium-to-high ticket education and consulting product sales. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business is indicated, assume online education with a main offer between 297 and 997 USD; if no platform is specified, assume use of a basic webinar tool (Zoom, EverWebinar, or unlisted YouTube); the webinar should be between 45 and 75 minutes long; proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste the business description, main offer to sell in the webinar, target audience, and main transformation promised. STEPS: 1. Define the webinar hook and promise (what the attendee will learn and why it matters now). 2. Design the registration page with copy: headline, subtitle, list of learnings, CTA, and urgency. 3. Create a 3-email pre-webinar sequence (confirmation, 24h reminder, 1h reminder). 4. Structure the webinar script in 6 blocks: opening/hook, credibility story, value content (3 key ideas), transition to the offer, offer presentation, close with urgency. 5. Design a 5-email post-webinar sequence: replay + scarcity, objection #1, objection #2, last day, close. 6. Define funnel metrics: registration rate, show-up rate, offer click-through rate, purchase conversion rate, value per attendee. OUTPUT: document per section with ready copy; metrics table with benchmarks; technical implementation checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) cold audience with no prior relationship → add a 5-7 day warm-up stage before the webinar; (b) ticket above 2,000 USD → replace direct webinar sale with a discovery call as the CTA; (c) low show-up rate → prioritize improvement of pre-webinar emails and add SMS. [C · CRITERIA] The webinar script must follow an 80% value / 20% sales ratio. The post-webinar sequence must not last more than 7 days. DoD: the team can have the funnel technically active in under one week.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that the transition from content to offer in the script is organic and not abrupt before delivering.
spec-marketing_mapa_micro_macro_conversi:
[S · SITUATION] A digital business measures only its final conversion (purchase or registration), which prevents it from identifying where in the funnel it is losing prospects and why. It lacks a map that distinguishes between micro conversions (intermediate actions that indicate progression) and the macro conversion (the primary business objective), making optimization decisions slow and imprecise. [P · REQUEST] Deliver a complete micro and macro conversion map for the funnel with an operational definition of each conversion, expected rate per step, diagnosis of probable leak points, and an instrumentation plan to measure them correctly. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a digital marketing analyst and web analytics and measurement specialist with experience designing conversion architectures for online education, SaaS, and e-commerce businesses. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business is indicated, assume an online education or consulting business with a content → lead magnet → offer funnel; if no analytics tool is specified, assume Google Analytics 4 or equivalent; proceed declaring these assumptions. INPUTS: paste the business description, primary business objective (macro conversion), current user flow from first contact to purchase, and available analytics tools. STEPS: 1. Define the macro conversion with the exact metric (e.g., completed purchase, signed contract, active subscription). 2. Map the funnel micro conversions from top to bottom (e.g., landing page visit, lead magnet download, email open, offer click, checkout start). 3. Assign expected conversion rate per step with a reference benchmark. 4. Calculate the volume required at the top of the funnel to reach the monthly sales goal. 5. Identify the 3 most probable leak points with root cause hypotheses. 6. Propose the instrumentation plan: events to track, recommended tool, minimum configuration. OUTPUT: map table with columns: Step, Type (micro/macro), Definition, Expected Rate, Benchmark; required volume calculation; leak points table with hypotheses; instrumentation checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) funnel with paid traffic → add a traffic source segmentation layer to the map; (b) business with multiple products → create one map per priority product line; (c) no analytics installed → prioritize tool configuration before optimizing conversions. [C · CRITERIA] Each micro conversion must be measurable without advanced development. The map must allow the highest-impact optimization point to be identified in under 5 minutes of review. DoD: the team can review the funnel status in a 15-minute weekly meeting using the map.

Protocolo MetodologIA: verify that each micro conversion is independently measurable and has an associated benchmark before delivering the map.
spec-marketing_diagnostico_fugas_embudo: [S · SITUATION] A B2B or B2C marketing team has been running a digital conversion funnel (awareness → consideration → decision → retention) for at least 3 months and has traffic, lead, opportunity and close metrics available. They detect that final results do not reflect entry volume and suspect leakage at specific stages, but have not yet quantified or located the bottlenecks. [P · REQUEST] Produce a funnel leakage diagnostic report that identifies the stages with the highest percentage loss, the probable root causes and a prioritized action plan with measurable corrective actions for the 3 most critical stages. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a senior conversion funnel optimization specialist with experience in CRO, web analytics and marketing automation. ASSUMPTIONS: if the user does not paste data, assume standard stages (Visitors → Leads → MQL → SQL → Close) with typical B2B conversion rates (2-5% visitor-to-lead, 20-30% lead-to-MQL, 40-60% MQL-to-SQL, 20-30% SQL-to-close); declare each assumption. Ask for real data only if confidence < 0.85 on a specific stage (max. 2 questions). INPUTS: funnel metrics pasted in the thread (volumes per stage, conversion rates, analysis period). STEPS: 1. Build a comparative table of actual vs. benchmark rates for each transition → 2. Calculate the leakage index (%) and estimated lost volume per stage → 3. Rank stages by impact (leakage × average opportunity value) → 4. Formulate 2-3 root-cause hypotheses per critical stage (data, UX, message, process) → 5. Propose 1 priority corrective action per stage with a success metric and timeline → 6. Write an executive summary ≤ 120 words. OUTPUT: (a) Leakage table by stage, (b) ranking of critical stages, (c) root-cause hypotheses, (d) action plan with placeholder responsible party, metric and timeline, (e) executive summary. EDGE CASES: (1) if only 2 stages are available, analyze the single transition and warn of the limitation; (2) if rates exceed benchmarks at every stage, redirect the diagnosis toward entry volume and audience quality; (3) if data spans different periods, normalize to weeks and notify. [C · CRITERIA] Each leakage must be expressed as both % and absolute volume. Root causes must include at least one data-based hypothesis and one behavior-based hypothesis. Actions must include a measurable metric. DoD: complete table + minimum 3 corrective actions + executive summary delivered.
spec-marketing_buyer_persona_basada_dato: [S · SITUATION] A company wants to move away from intuitive or generic customer profiles and build buyer personas backed by real data: interviews, surveys, web behavior, CRM or reviews. EDGE CASES: (a) If the brief is B2B, focus the cultural tension on the world of the purchase decision-maker, not the mass consumer; (b) if the brand is a challenger with a small budget, prioritize concepts that generate earned media and organic virality; (c) if the product is regulated (finance, health), verify the concept makes no specific results claims. [C · CRITERIA] The big idea must be expressible in a single sentence; the concept must be applicable to at least 5 different formats without losing coherence; the tagline must be memorable and ownable for the brand; DoD: territories evaluated, big idea developed in all its elements, multichannel application described. Protocolo MetodologIA: before presenting, verify that the big idea resolves the insight's tension and is differentiating relative to its category.
spec-marketing_plan_lanzamiento_gtm: [S · SITUATION] A company is about to launch a new product or service and needs a structured go-to-market (GTM) plan organized by phases that coordinates positioning, channels, messages, teams, and success metrics. Without this plan, sales, marketing, and product efforts operate in silos and the launch fails to maximize the window of opportunity. [P · REQUEST] Build a phased GTM launch plan from pre-launch through post-launch with results review, including activities, owners, channels, messages, and KPIs per phase. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a VP of Marketing specializing in B2B and B2C product launches, with experience at high-growth startups and corporate companies. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business model is stated, assume SaaS or digital product and declare it; if no budget is stated, assume a lean launch and prioritize organic and low-cost channels; if no timeline is stated, assume 12 total weeks (4 pre + 2 launch + 6 post); proceed declaring assumptions, only ask if there is no defined product or target market. INPUTS: product description, target market, and business objectives pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define central positioning and key messages for each segment. 2. Structure phases: Pre-launch (awareness and anticipation), Launch (activation and conversion), Post-launch (retention and expansion). 3. For each phase: list concrete activities (verb + observable result), channels, responsible team, execution week, and associated KPI. 4. Build a launch milestones table with relative dates (week 1, week 2, etc.). 5. Identify launch risks and contingency plans. 6. Define success criteria at 30, 60, and 90 days. OUTPUT: GTM document with: (a) positioning and messages summary (1 page), (b) phases table with activities, owners, and KPIs, (c) milestones table, (d) risk register with mitigation, (e) 30/60/90-day success scorecard. Tabular format where applicable. EDGE CASES: (a) If launching in multiple markets simultaneously, add a column per market in the phases table; (b) if the product is in closed beta, add an early-adopter feedback phase before the public launch; (c) if the team is a single person, simplify owners and prioritize the 3 highest-impact activities per phase. [C · CRITERIA] Each activity must have a verb, a result, and a week; KPIs must be measurable without paid tools; the plan must work without dependence on a mass-media budget; DoD: all three phases completed with at least 4 activities each, success scorecard defined. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that each KPI has a measurement method and that critical milestones have contingency plans.
spec-marketing_plan_campana_360: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team needs to coordinate an advertising campaign that operates coherently and synergistically across multiple channels: paid media, owned media, earned media, and experiential. Without 360 orchestration, each channel broadcasts different messages, efforts are duplicated, and the consumer experience is fragmented. [P · REQUEST] Develop a complete integrated 360 multichannel campaign plan with per-channel strategy, activation calendar, indicative budget per channel, and a unified measurement system. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are an integrated marketing director with 10 years of experience coordinating 360 campaigns for mass-consumer and B2B brands, expert in orchestrating paid, owned, and earned media synergistically. ASSUMPTIONS: if no total budget is stated, assume an indicative distribution (40% paid media, 30% production, 20% experiential, 10% PR) and declare it as an assumption; if no duration is stated, assume 8 weeks; if no channels are stated, include: paid social media, SEO/content, email marketing, OOH, PR, and experiential activation; proceed without asking unless there is no brand and no defined objective. INPUTS: brief or campaign description pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define message architecture: central message and adaptations per channel. 2. For each channel: specific objective, content format, frequency, primary KPI, and owner. 3. Design the activation sequence: which channel activates first and how each feeds the next (customer journey). 4. Build a week-by-week campaign calendar (table). 5. Estimate budget distribution by channel (percentages). 6. Define the measurement system: per-channel metrics + unified campaign metric (e.g. total reach, attributed conversions). 7. Include a weekly optimization mechanism (what to review and how to adjust). OUTPUT: 360 plan document with: (a) message architecture, (b) channel profile table, (c) activation calendar (week × channel table), (d) budget distribution (table), (e) measurement system and optimization mechanism. EDGE CASES: (a) If the budget is very tight (<20,000 USD), drop OOH and experiential and concentrate on digital owned + PR; (b) if the product is a niche B2B, replace mass social networks with LinkedIn and technical content marketing; (c) if the campaign has a crisis or politically sensitive component, add a message approval protocol before publishing. [C · CRITERIA] Each channel must have a differentiated, non-redundant KPI; the activation sequence must clearly show how channels reinforce one another; the calendar must be executable by a team of 3–5 people; DoD: all channels documented, full calendar, measurement system defined. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that the central message is coherent across all channels and that there is no overlap between channel KPIs.
spec-marketing_campana_estacional_calend: [S · SITUATION] A brand needs to plan its marketing campaigns in advance to capitalize on the commercial and seasonal dates of the year (seasons, festivities, industry events) that represent demand peaks or heightened consumer attention. The lack of a consolidated seasonal calendar leads to late reactions, rushed production, and lost competitive opportunities. [P · REQUEST] Build an annual calendar of seasonal campaigns and key dates for the indicated brand, with activation planning per date, differentiated messages, channels, and minimum recommended production lead time. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a calendar marketing planning expert with experience in retail, e-commerce, and mass-consumer brands, specializing in maximizing performance on peak dates. ASSUMPTIONS: if no geographic market is stated, assume Mexico or Spanish-speaking Latin America and declare it; if no category is stated, infer from the brand name and declare it; if no budget per date is stated, prioritize the 5 highest-impact dates for the category; proceed without asking unless no brand and no identifiable industry exist. INPUTS: brand name, product category, and market pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the 12–18 most relevant commercial and seasonal dates for the category and market. 2. For each date: occasion name, activation window (weeks before the event), communication objective, differentiated message, recommended channels, primary content format, and expected KPI. 3. Build a visual calendar (month × date table) with priority indicators (High / Medium / Low). 4. Add production lead-time recommendations (minimum time to approve and produce each type of piece). 5. Identify 3 unconventional or culturally relevant date opportunities that competitors typically ignore. 6. Include a seasonal pre-campaign checklist (10 items). OUTPUT: Seasonal calendar document with: (a) dates table with all fields, (b) visual month × date calendar with priorities, (c) production lead-time recommendations, (d) unconventional opportunities, (e) pre-campaign checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) If the brand operates in multiple countries, add a regional-variation column for dates that differ; (b) if the category is B2B, replace consumer festivities with fiscal-cycle dates, industry conferences, and contract-renewal periods; (c) if the team is small, mark the 5 dates with the highest expected ROI with an asterisk to prioritize resources. [C · CRITERIA] Each date must have a differentiated message (not generic); production lead time must be realistic based on the type of piece; unconventional opportunities must be specific to the category; DoD: minimum 12 dates documented, full visual calendar, checklist delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that messages per date are consistent with brand positioning and that high-priority dates have sufficient lead time.
spec-marketing_secuencia_pre_lanzamiento: [S · SITUATION] A brand is preparing to launch a product, service, or collection and wants to build anticipation, desire, and organic conversation before the official launch date. Without an orchestrated pre-launch sequence, launch day arrives with no prepared audience, no waitlist, and no spontaneous coverage. [P · REQUEST] Design a tactical pre-launch sequence to generate hype and anticipation during the weeks leading up to the launch, specifying each action, channel, content, timing, and success metric. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a growth marketer specialized in product launches with experience in viral anticipation campaigns for consumer and technology brands. ASSUMPTIONS: if no pre-launch timeline is stated, assume 4 weeks; if no primary channel is stated, assume Instagram + email + PR; if no waitlist incentive is stated, propose early access or an exclusive first-buyer discount; proceed declaring assumptions without asking, unless there is no product and no launch date. INPUTS: product description and launch date pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the central hype hook: what makes the product worthy of anticipation (differentiator, scarcity, novelty). 2. Design the week-by-week sequence with: week, action type (teaser / partial reveal / social proof / countdown), channel, content format, suggested copy or creative direction, and tracking metric. 3. Specify the waitlist or interest-registration mechanic: platform, incentive, nurturing email flow. 4. Design 2–3 amplification moments (influencer unboxing, beta tester testimonial, surprise reveal). 5. Define an engagement response protocol for comments and interactions during pre-launch. 6. Set pre-launch success thresholds (e.g. minimum registrations, engagement rate). OUTPUT: Pre-launch sequence document with: (a) central hype hook, (b) week × action × channel × content × metric sequence table, (c) waitlist mechanic with nurturing flow, (d) amplification plan, (e) response protocol, (f) success thresholds. EDGE CASES: (a) If the product already has a leak or prior rumor, adapt the sequence to capitalize on the rumor rather than ignore it; (b) if the audience is B2B, replace mass-hype tactics with an exclusive early-access webinar and case study preview; (c) if the budget is minimal, build the sequence entirely on organic channels and micro-influencer co-creation. [C · CRITERIA] The sequence must scale gradually in the level of product revelation; each action must have a specific, non-generic metric; the waitlist mechanic must include at least 2 nurturing emails; DoD: complete week-by-week sequence, waitlist mechanic documented, success thresholds defined. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that the sequence builds progressive narrative tension and that success thresholds are achievable with the declared audience.
spec-marketing_plan_account_based_market: [S · SITUATION] A B2B marketing team needs to design an account-based marketing (ABM) strategy to concentrate resources on high-value target accounts rather than generating an indiscriminate volume of leads. Without a structured ABM plan, marketing and sales efforts are misaligned, messages are generic, and the sales cycle at enterprise accounts is endless. [P · REQUEST] Build a complete ABM campaign plan for the indicated target accounts, including account selection, stakeholder map, personalized messages by role, activation tactics, and account-progress tracking system. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are an ABM strategist with experience in B2B enterprise sales, specializing in aligning marketing and sales to penetrate high-value accounts in technology, financial, and industrial sectors. ASSUMPTIONS: if no ABM tier (1-to-1, 1-to-few, 1-to-many) is stated, assume 1-to-few with 5–10 target accounts and declare it; if no sales cycle is stated, assume 3–6 months; if no decision-maker roles are stated, assume C-suite + technical champion + end user; proceed declaring assumptions without asking, unless no industry and no B2B product are identified. INPUTS: B2B product/service description, target industry, and any target account information pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define target account selection criteria (ICP: firmographics, buying signals, revenue potential). 2. Build a stakeholder map per account: role, influence, interest, primary pain point, and personalized message. 3. Design an activation sequence by funnel stage: account awareness, stakeholder engagement, opportunity acceleration. 4. Select tactics by stage: personalized content, 1-to-1 events, multichannel outreach (LinkedIn, email, phone), targeted ads. 5. Define an account scoring system with progress criteria. 6. Establish a marketing-sales review cadence (smarketing): frequency, agenda, and alignment metrics. 7. Design an ABM tracking dashboard: pipeline metrics, account engagement, and opportunity velocity. OUTPUT: ABM plan document with: (a) ICP criteria and target account list, (b) stakeholder map (account × role × message table), (c) activation sequence by stage with tactics, (d) account scoring system, (e) marketing-sales review cadence, (f) ABM metrics dashboard. EDGE CASES: (a) If the target account is already in the sales funnel, design acceleration tactics rather than awareness tactics; (b) if the team has no dedicated ABM tool, build the system on LinkedIn Sales Navigator + HubSpot or equivalent; (c) if there are multiple target industries, create a plan per vertical with differentiated messages. [C · CRITERIA] Each stakeholder must have a message personalized to their pain point (not generic); the account score must have objective, weighted criteria; the marketing-sales cadence must include a sample agenda; DoD: full stakeholder map, activation sequence by stage, metrics dashboard defined. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that messages per role are differentiated and that the account scoring system has unambiguous measurable criteria.
spec-marketing_modelo_mensaje_campana_ai: [S · SITUATION] A marketing or sales team needs to structure the messages of a campaign or commercial communication using the AIDA model (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) to maximize the persuasive effectiveness of copy in each piece or channel. Messages without a persuasive structure lose the reader in the first few lines and fail to generate the desired action. [P · REQUEST] Write the complete AIDA message structure for the indicated campaign or communication, with specific copy for each stage, per-channel adaptations, and an application guide. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a strategic copywriter with 10 years of experience in direct-response copy and conversion campaigns, specializing in applying persuasive frameworks such as AIDA to increase conversion rates. ASSUMPTIONS: if no channel is stated, develop a master AIDA version and then adapt it for email, social media, and landing page; if no audience is stated, infer from the product and declare it; if no conversion objective is stated, assume registration/lead as the final action; proceed declaring assumptions without asking, unless no product and no identifiable audience exist. INPUTS: product/service description, audience, and conversion objective pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the most powerful attention hook for the audience (pain point, curiosity, promise). 2. For each AIDA stage: write a specific copy block with usage instructions and variants. (A) Attention: main headline + 2 alternatives (max. 10 words each). (I) Interest: paragraph developing the problem or need (50–80 words). (D) Desire: paragraph presenting the solution and its emotional and rational benefits (60–100 words). (A) Action: main CTA + 2 alternatives with an urgency or scarcity instruction where applicable. 3. Build per-channel message versions: email (subject + body), social media post (short version ≤280 characters), landing page (above the fold). 4. Include copy notes: which words and phrases power each stage and why. 5. Add an AIDA validation checklist (7 questions to review before publishing). OUTPUT: AIDA messages document with: (a) attention hook analysis, (b) copy blocks per stage with variants, (c) per-channel adaptations (table), (d) copy notes with justification, (e) AIDA validation checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) If the product is low emotional-involvement (commodity), reinforce the Desire stage with social proof and a guarantee; (b) if the channel is B2B cold email, the Attention stage must reference a specific business pain point, not an emotional promise; (c) if there are multiple audience segments, create one AIDA block per segment with a differentiated hook. [C · CRITERIA] The headline must be readable and understandable in under 3 seconds; the CTA must contain an imperative verb and an implicit benefit; per-channel adaptations must respect each platform's character limits; DoD: four AIDA stages with complete copy, per-channel adaptations delivered, checklist included. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that there is a single primary action in stage A (Action) and that the AIDA flow is coherent from beginning to end.
spec-marketing_plan_partnership_co_marke: [S · SITUATION] Two complementary (non-competing) brands want to develop a co-marketing campaign that amplifies both brands' reach, shares costs, and creates additional value for shared audiences. Without a structured co-marketing plan, responsibilities become blurred, brand messages contaminate each other, and the campaign ends up benefiting one partner disproportionately. [P · REQUEST] Build a complete co-marketing plan for the indicated alliance, including governance structure, division of responsibilities, co-branded messages, joint activities, and shared success metrics. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a strategic marketing alliance specialist with experience designing and executing co-marketing campaigns between consumer, technology, and professional-services brands. ASSUMPTIONS: if no duration is indicated, assume a 6–8-week campaign; if no co-branding format is indicated, assume balanced presence from both brands with no dominant primary brand; if no channel is indicated, propose the channel where both brands' audiences overlap most; proceed by declaring assumptions without asking, unless no two identifiable brands or joint product/service can be found. INPUTS: description of both brands, joint product or service, shared target audience, and alliance objective. STEPS: 1. Analyze complementarity: what each brand contributes (audience, credibility, distribution, content). 2. Define shared objective and success metrics per brand (they may differ). 3. Design the co-branding architecture: visual hierarchy, alliance umbrella message, and differentiated messages per brand. 4. Build the joint activity plan: webinar, co-created content, combined offer, event, etc., with an owner per activity (Brand A / Brand B / Both). 5. Establish governance structure: decisions that require joint vs. unilateral approval, communication channel between teams, review frequency. 6. Design the audience-exchange mechanism: how each brand presents the other without surrendering its database. 7. Define a contingency plan for creative or messaging disagreements. OUTPUT: Co-marketing plan document with: (a) complementarity analysis, (b) objectives and metrics per brand, (c) co-branding architecture, (d) joint activity table (activity, owner, channel, date, KPI), (e) governance structure, (f) audience-exchange mechanism, (g) contingency plan. EDGE CASES: (a) If one brand has greater equity, explicitly state that the lesser brand will not be subordinated in materials; (b) if audiences are distinct (no overlap), reframe as market-extension co-marketing rather than mutual reinforcement; (c) if the alliance is long-term, add renewal criteria and alliance health metrics. [C · CRITERIA] Responsibilities must be specific per brand and unambiguous; success metrics must be independently measurable by each brand; the co-branding architecture must protect both brands' identities; DoD: all sections completed, activity table with dates and owners, governance documented. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that success metrics are equitable for both brands and that responsibilities have no unassigned overlaps.
spec-marketing_post_mortem_campana: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team has just concluded a campaign and needs to systematically analyze what worked, what did not, why, and what concrete changes to apply in the next campaign. Without a structured post-mortem, errors repeat, successes are forgotten, and the organization fails to build cumulative marketing intelligence. [P · REQUEST] Facilitate and write a complete post-mortem analysis of the indicated campaign, with evaluation of results vs. objectives, root-cause diagnosis, actionable learnings, and recommendations for future campaigns. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are an analytical marketing director with experience in campaign retrospectives and in building organizational learning systems in high-performance marketing teams. ASSUMPTIONS: if no actual result data are provided, structure the post-mortem as a guided template with facilitator questions and fields to complete; if no campaign duration is indicated, assume a 4–8-week campaign; if no original KPIs are documented, request them as the only critical missing data point before continuing; proceed by declaring assumptions for everything else. INPUTS: original campaign objectives, results obtained, performance data by channel, and any team observations pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Compare results obtained vs. original SMART objectives (traffic-light table: green/yellow/red per KPI). 2. Analyze performance by channel: which channel exceeded expectations, which disappointed, which was neutral. 3. Identify the 3 biggest campaign wins with evidence and success factor. 4. Identify the 3 biggest failures or improvement areas with root-cause diagnosis (tool: 5 whys or simplified Ishikawa). 5. Extract actionable learnings: what to do differently next time, in what format and at what point. 6. Write prioritized recommendations for the next campaign (table: recommendation, expected impact, effort, priority). 7. Define 2–3 hypotheses to test in the next campaign based on the learnings. OUTPUT: Post-mortem document with: (a) KPI traffic-light table, (b) performance analysis by channel, (c) wins section with evidence, (d) failures section with root cause, (e) prioritized recommendations table, (f) hypotheses to test. Tone: constructive and solution-oriented, not punitive. EDGE CASES: (a) If results are partial or incomplete, document data limitations and use estimated ranges with an uncertainty note; (b) if external factors impacted results (seasonality, crisis, competition), isolate them as external variables before diagnosing internal causes; (c) if the team is demoralized by poor results, structure the document starting with wins before failures. [C · CRITERIA] Each learning must be actionable and specific (not "improve the content" but "increase LinkedIn posting frequency from 2 to 4 posts/week"); root causes must be verified with evidence or declared as hypotheses; DoD: complete traffic-light table, minimum 3 wins and 3 failures with root cause, recommendations table with priority. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that each recommendation is linked to a specific learning and that none is generic without supporting evidence.
spec-marketing_modelo_atribucion_multito: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team invests in multiple simultaneous channels (search, social, email, display, organic) and does not know what percentage of credit for each conversion belongs to each channel or touchpoint. Without a defined multitouch attribution model, investment decisions default to last-click, which undervalues top-of-funnel channels and leads to suboptimal budget allocation. [P · REQUEST] Design a multitouch attribution model appropriate for the described marketing ecosystem, with model definition, implementation methodology, credit criteria by touchpoint, recommended tools, and validation plan. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a data-driven marketing analyst specializing in attribution and measurement, with experience implementing attribution models for companies with media budgets of 100K to 5M USD annually. ASSUMPTIONS: if no technology stack is indicated, assume Google Analytics 4 + basic CRM and declare it; if no conversion volume is indicated, assume medium volume (500–2,000 conversions/month) and recommend a statistical or data-driven model; if no industry is indicated, infer from the product type and declare it; proceed without asking unless no marketing channels or conversion objective can be identified. INPUTS: active marketing channels, conversion objective, available measurement stack, and any data constraints. STEPS: 1. Analyze the customer journey map: list typical touchpoints from awareness to conversion and post-conversion. 2. Evaluate available attribution models (last click, first click, linear, time decay, position-based, data-driven) with pros/cons for the specific case. 3. Recommend the most appropriate model and justify the choice with objective criteria. 4. Define the implementation methodology: how to track each touchpoint, what data to collect, recommended attribution window. 5. Establish credit weights per touchpoint in the chosen model (table). 6. Recommend technology stack to implement the model with options by budget. 7. Design a validation plan: how to determine whether the model is more accurate than the current model, suggested incrementality test. 8. Include known model limitations and how to mitigate them. OUTPUT: Attribution model design document with: (a) customer journey map with touchpoints, (b) model comparison table, (c) recommended model with justification, (d) implementation methodology, (e) credit weight table, (f) technology stack recommendations, (g) validation plan, (h) limitations and mitigations section. EDGE CASES: (a) If there are privacy constraints (iOS 14+, cookieless), include cookie-free measurement alternatives (conversion modeling, Privacy Sandbox); (b) if conversion volume is low (<200/month), recommend a heuristic (non-statistical) model and explain why; (c) if there are offline channels (sales rep, event, store), include an offline data integration methodology. [C · CRITERIA] The recommended model must be justified with objective criteria from the case (volume, channels, purchase cycle); credit weights must sum to 100%; the validation plan must include a comparison metric between the current and new model; DoD: all sections complete, model comparison table, weights table, and validation plan delivered. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that credit weights sum to 100% and that model limitations are documented with their mitigation.
spec-marketing_dashboard_kpis_marketing: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team needs to design a KPI dashboard that enables real-time or periodic monitoring of all marketing activity performance, aligns the team around the metrics that matter, and facilitates data-driven decision-making. Without a structured dashboard, the team reports vanity metrics, executives have no real visibility into performance, and weeks are lost debating what measures success. [P · REQUEST] Design a complete marketing KPI dashboard, with metric definitions by level (executive, tactical, operational), data sources, update frequency, and visualization specifications per metric. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: You are a marketing analyst and data visualization expert with experience designing marketing dashboards for teams of 5 to 50 people using tools such as Looker Studio, Power BI, HubSpot, or Tableau. ASSUMPTIONS: if no visualization tool is indicated, recommend Looker Studio (free) as the primary option; if no industry is indicated, infer from the product type and declare it; if no dashboard audience is indicated, design for three levels (C-suite, marketing management, operational team); proceed by declaring assumptions without asking, unless no marketing objective or identifiable channels exist. INPUTS: marketing objective, active channels, and available measurement tools pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Define the business objectives the dashboard must answer (3–5 key questions). 2. Structure the dashboard in 3 levels: (a) Executive: 5–7 business KPIs (revenue, CAC, LTV, marketing ROI, share of voice); (b) Tactical: 8–12 metrics by channel and funnel stage; (c) Operational: active campaign metrics and performance alerts. 3. Per KPI: exact name, exact definition, calculation formula, data source, update frequency, recommended visualization type, and alert threshold (green/yellow/red). 4. Design the data architecture: where data comes from, how it is integrated, and what automations are needed. 5. Specify the visual design of the dashboard: section layout, color palette, information hierarchy. 6. Define the dashboard review cadence: weekly team meeting, monthly leadership review, automatic alerts. OUTPUT: Dashboard design document with: (a) key questions to answer, (b) KPI table by level (name, definition, formula, source, frequency, visualization, thresholds), (c) data architecture, (d) visual design specifications, (e) review cadence and alert protocol. EDGE CASES: (a) If the team has no dedicated analyst, simplify to 10–12 total KPIs and automate all possible updates; (b) if there are multiple business units or markets, add segmentation filters to the dashboard; (c) if the company is in early stage and has no historical data, include an industry benchmarks section as an initial reference. [C · CRITERIA] Each KPI must have an explicit calculation formula and an identified data source; alert thresholds must be based on historical data or declared benchmarks; the executive dashboard must have no more than 7 metrics; DoD: KPI table complete for all 3 levels, data architecture documented, review cadence defined. Protocolo MetodologIA: before delivering, verify that there are no vanity metrics without a business objective link and that every KPI has a data source reachable with the available stack.
spec-marketing_calculo_cac_ltv_ratio:
[S · SITUATION] A digital subscription company (SaaS, recurring ecommerce, or membership service) needs to know whether its customer acquisition is financially sustainable. The marketing and finance team has historical campaign data, customer cohorts, and income statements, but has not yet consolidated per-customer profitability metrics into a single framework. [P · REQUEST] Calculate Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC), Customer Lifetime Value (LTV), and the LTV:CAC ratio from the provided data; interpret whether the business is profitable per customer; and identify improvement levers. The deliverable is a structured table with formulas explained, a diagnostic paragraph, and at least 3 prioritized recommendations. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior unit-economics analyst with experience in subscription models and per-segment profitability. ASSUMPTIONS: if marketing costs by channel are not indicated, consolidate total marketing and sales spend for the period; if monthly churn rate is not indicated, infer from cohort data or assume 5% monthly and declare it; if gross margin is not specified, assume 70% for SaaS or 40% for physical ecommerce. INPUTS: paste below the available data (marketing/sales spend per period, number of new customers, average revenue per customer, churn rate or retention cohort, estimated gross margin). STEPS: 1. Calculate CAC = Total marketing+sales spend / New customers in the same period; break down by channel if data available. 2. Calculate LTV using the gross-margin model: LTV = (ARPU × Gross margin) / Monthly churn; show explicit formula. 3. Calculate LTV:CAC ratio and compare against benchmarks (healthy ≥ 3:1, critical < 1:1). 4. Calculate CAC payback period in months. 5. Produce summary table and narrative diagnosis. 6. List improvement levers ordered by potential impact. OUTPUT: table with fields (Metric, Calculated value, Formula, Reference benchmark) + 80–120-word diagnosis + list of 3–5 recommendations with target metric. EDGE CASES: (a) if the ratio is negative due to negative margins, flag it as a critical alert and refer to cost-structure analysis; (b) if data are insufficient to calculate churn, present a scenario range (optimistic/base/pessimistic); (c) if there are multiple customer segments, calculate metrics per segment and not just the aggregate. [C · CRITERIA] All formulas are explicit and reproducible; the LTV:CAC ratio has a qualitative interpretation; recommendations have concrete target metrics; no figures are invented without marking them [ASSUMPTION]. DoD: complete table, diagnosis written, minimum 3 recommendations with metric.

Protocolo MetodologIA: declare assumptions before calculating, mark each inferred figure with [ASSUMPTION], and present at least one alternative scenario if data are partial.
spec-marketing_analisis_cohortes_retenci:
[S · SITUATION] A digital product (mobile app, SaaS platform, or subscription service) wants to understand how it retains users over time. The product and marketing team has user registration and activity data, but so far only looks at aggregate metrics that hide differences between generations of users. A cohort analysis is needed to reveal real patterns of retention, churn, and recovery. [P · REQUEST] Build a retention cohort table, trace the retention curves by cohort, identify the inflection point where retention stabilizes ("natural retention"), and extract actionable conclusions about which generations of users retain better and why. The deliverable is the formatted cohort table, the curves described or plotted, and a narrative analysis with at least 3 findings and 3 causal hypotheses with a validation recommendation. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Data scientist specializing in user-behavior and retention analysis for digital products. ASSUMPTIONS: if no time window is specified, use retention at 1, 7, 14, 30, and 90 days for mobile apps, or monthly retention for SaaS; if no "retention" event is indicated, assume login or active use according to product context; if data are in raw format, describe how to preprocess them before continuing. INPUTS: paste below the user event table (user_id, registration date, activity dates) or an already-calculated cohort table. STEPS: 1. Group users by registration cohort (week or month depending on volume). 2. Calculate retention rate per cohort for each period: (active users in period N / total users in that cohort) × 100. 3. Organize into a cohort × period matrix and calculate averages by period. 4. Identify the cohort with the highest retention in each period and the one with the lowest. 5. Detect the period where the curve flattens (natural retention). 6. Compare cohorts from different eras to detect improvements or degradations in the product. 7. Write findings and formulate hypotheses with a suggested experiment to validate each one. OUTPUT: cohort table with percentage values, averages row, and best/worst cohorts row; curve description with inflection point identification; narrative analysis with 3 labeled findings and 3 hypotheses with suggested experiment. EDGE CASES: (a) if cohort size is fewer than 30 users, mark as statistically unstable; (b) if there are seasonal events distorting specific cohorts, flag them as anomalies; (c) if period-1 retention is below 20%, escalate as a critical onboarding alert before continuing. [C · CRITERIA] The table is complete and percentages are internally coherent; each finding has evidence in the data; each hypothesis has a concrete and feasible experiment; causality is not asserted without evidence. DoD: complete cohort table, minimum 3 findings, minimum 3 hypotheses with experiment.

Protocolo MetodologIA: separate findings (what the data says) from hypotheses (why it might be so) and label each causal claim as [HYPOTHESIS] until validated.
spec-marketing_plan_medicion_kpi_tree:
[S · SITUATION] A marketing team at a digital company needs to move from measuring activities (impressions, clicks, posts) to measuring business results in a structured way. Current dashboards are filled with disconnected metrics and no one can trace the line between a tactical action and revenue impact. Leadership demands greater accountability and traceability. [P · REQUEST] Design a complete measurement plan with a KPI tree that connects the main business objective (North Star Metric) to intermediate result metrics, process metrics, and activity metrics. The deliverable is a 3–4-level hierarchical tree, a technical card per key KPI (definition, formula, frequency, owner, data source), and a prioritization guide to know what to monitor first. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Marketing analytics consultant with experience designing results-oriented measurement systems. ASSUMPTIONS: if no business objective is specified, assume recurring-revenue growth as the North Star; if no business model is indicated, infer from context and declare it; if no measurement tools are mentioned, design the tree platform-agnostic. INPUTS: describe below the business (model, audience, primary channels), the strategic objective for the period, and the metrics currently tracked. STEPS: 1. Identify the North Star Metric that best represents the value delivered to the customer and business growth. 2. Decompose into 2–4 business-result metrics (revenue, retention, macro conversion). 3. For each result metric, identify 2–3 process metrics (behaviors that drive it). 4. For each process metric, identify 1–2 activity metrics (measurable tactical actions). 5. Build the hierarchical tree with hypothetical causal arrows. 6. Produce technical cards for the 5–7 most critical KPIs. 7. Prioritize which metrics to instrument first based on data availability and expected impact. OUTPUT: KPI tree in hierarchical text format with 3–4 levels; technical cards table (Name, Definition, Formula, Target, Frequency, Owner, Source); instrumentation priority ranking with justification. EDGE CASES: (a) if a dashboard already exists, evaluate which metrics to keep, which to discontinue, and which to add; (b) if the business model has multiple segments with different North Stars, build sub-trees per segment; (c) if there is conflict between vanity metrics and result metrics, flag it explicitly and propose the substitution. [C · CRITERIA] Each KPI has an explicit formula; causality between levels is reasonable and declared as [HYPOTHESIS]; the tree has complete vertical coherence from activity to business result; the prioritization ranking is actionable the following week. DoD: complete 3–4-level tree, 5–7 KPI cards, prioritization ranking.

Protocolo MetodologIA: declare the North Star Metric first and build the tree top-down, labeling causal relationships as [HYPOTHESIS] until data confirm them.
spec-marketing_diseno_ab_test_significan:
[S · SITUATION] A product or marketing team wants to launch a controlled experiment (A/B test) to make an evidence-based decision: change an element of a landing page, email copy, onboarding flow, or another variation. The team has historical data on the conversion metric and wants to ensure the experiment is statistically well-designed before executing it, to avoid false conclusions from insufficient samples or inadequate duration. [P · REQUEST] Design the complete A/B experiment: define null and alternative hypotheses, calculate the minimum required sample size, estimate experiment duration given available traffic, establish stopping criteria, and produce the analysis protocol. The deliverable is an experiment design document with all statistical parameters justified and an execution checklist. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Experimentation statistician with experience designing and analyzing A/B tests in digital product and marketing environments. ASSUMPTIONS: use significance level α=0.05 and statistical power β=0.80 unless another value is indicated; if no primary metric is specified, use conversion rate; if no minimum detectable effect is indicated, ask the team what percentage change justifies the experiment cost and use 10% as the declared default. INPUTS: describe below the element to test, the proposed variation, the primary metric, the historical conversion rate of the metric, and available average daily or weekly traffic. STEPS: 1. Write the null hypothesis (H0: no difference between A and B) and alternative (H1: variation B produces a change ≥ MDE in the metric). 2. Define the Minimum Detectable Effect (MDE) in absolute and relative terms. 3. Calculate the sample size per group using a proportions formula or t-test depending on the metric type; show the explicit calculation. 4. Estimate experiment duration in days: total size / daily traffic, adjusted for weekly cycles. 5. Define early-stopping criteria (peeking rules) and policy for correcting multiple-comparison bias if there are secondary variants. 6. Specify how the statistical analysis will be conducted at close: test to use, p-value and confidence interval calculation, business decision based on result. 7. Produce an execution checklist with owners. OUTPUT: document with sections: Hypotheses, Statistical parameters (α, β, MDE, n per group), Estimated duration, Stopping criteria, Analysis protocol, Execution checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) if available traffic makes duration exceed 6 weeks, alert about contamination risk and recommend reducing MDE ambition or limiting the experiment; (b) if there are multiple secondary metrics, specify Bonferroni or FDR correction; (c) if the base conversion rate is below 1%, recommend testing with higher-frequency intermediate metrics. [C · CRITERIA] Sample-size calculations are reproducible with the formulas shown; estimated duration accounts for weekly cycles; stopping criteria are defined before execution; the protocol does not allow "peeking" without statistical correction. DoD: all document sections complete, explicit calculations, checklist with owners.

Protocolo MetodologIA: define hypotheses and MDE before any calculation; document all chosen statistical parameters with their justification before executing the experiment.
spec-marketing_marketing_mix_modeling:
[S · SITUATION] A company with advertising spend distributed across multiple channels (paid search, social media, television, display, email, influencers, or others) needs to know what fraction of its sales or conversions can be attributed to each channel, separating the effect of marketing from organic growth, seasonality, and other external factors. Last-click or multitouch attribution models available on advertising platforms do not capture the impact of cookieless channels or the effect of offline channels. [P · REQUEST] Design and interpret a Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) that quantifies each channel's contribution to sales or conversions, estimates ROI per channel, and produces budget reallocation recommendations.
