Trade-off: cordiality vs. urgency → prioritize cordiality if the relationship spans >2 years, urgency if <10 days remain. DoD: subject + complete body, consistent tone, visible deadline, no unfilled placeholders. Protocolo MetodologIA: declare applied assumptions at the start of your response before showing the email.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_pitch_10_: [S · SITUATION] An entrepreneur, product leader, or sales executive needs to create a pitch deck for an audience of investors, directors, or strategic clients. They want to follow Guy Kawasaki's 10-20-30 rule: maximum 10 slides, 20 minutes of presentation, and minimum 30-point font. [P · REQUEST] Generate the complete pitch deck structure with: title of each slide, key content per slide (bullets or guide paragraph), assigned time, and recommended evidence source. Deliverable: table or structured list with the 10 slides, text for each, and timing. [E · EXECUTION] ROL: Senior strategic communication and investment pitch consultant with experience in seed rounds and C-level presentations. SUPUESTOS: if no business stage is indicated, assume early-stage startup seeking validation or seed investment [ASSUMPTION]; if no real financial data is available, indicate with [PENDING DATA] for the user to complete [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the product/company name and central problem are missing (confidence < 0.85). INSUMOS: the user will paste business context, problem, solution, market, and available traction. PASOS: 1. Identify the central value proposition → 1-sentence elevator pitch. 2. Map the 10 canonical Kawasaki slides to the specific context → list with personalized title. 3. Draft content for each slide (3-5 bullets or 40-60 words) → editable text. 4. Assign minutes to each slide summing to 20 min total → time column. 5. Recommend the type of evidence or visual for each slide → resource column. 6. Verify narrative coherence from start to finish → flow adjustment. SALIDA: table with columns No. | Slide Title | Key Content | Time (min) | Recommended Evidence. CASOS BORDE: (a) business without traction → prioritize validated hypotheses and market size; (b) technical audience → add architecture or technology slide within the product slot; (c) time limited to 10 min → compress to 10 slides at 1 minute each with minimal bullets. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: exactly 10 slides, sum of times = 20 min, no slide exceeds 60 words of content. Trade-off: depth vs. brevity → prioritize brevity; details go to the appendix. DoD: complete table without empty slides, without invented data not marked [PENDING DATA], coherent narrative flow. Protocolo MetodologIA: show the 1-sentence elevator pitch first before the slide table.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_apertura_: [S · SITUATION] A presenter needs to capture the audience's attention in the first 60-90 seconds of a presentation (internal, commercial, or at a conference). Without a powerful hook, the audience disconnects before reaching the relevant content. [P · REQUEST] Generate 3 opening variants with an impact hook for the same presentation, each using a distinct technique (surprising statistic, disruptive question, micro-story or future scenario). Deliverable: 3 complete openings of 60-90 seconds of reading (≈130-200 words each), labeled by technique. [E · EXECUTION] ROL: Oratory and persuasive communication coach with experience in TEDx and high-impact executive presentations. SUPUESTOS: if no audience is indicated, assume mid-to-senior-level executives in a corporate context [ASSUMPTION]; if no real statistics are available, the user will fill them in; mark with [PENDING STATISTIC] where applicable [ASSUMPTION]; if no total presentation duration is specified, assume 20 minutes [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the central topic of the presentation is missing (confidence < 0.85). INSUMOS: the user will paste the topic, audience, presentation objective, and any available data or story. PASOS: 1. Identify the central tension or paradox of the topic → 1 anchor phrase. 2. Draft opening type A: surprising statistic + emotional consequence → fluid text. 3. Draft opening type B: disruptive question with no obvious answer → fluid text. 4. Draft opening type C: micro-story or vivid second-person scenario → fluid text. 5. For each opening, add 1 transition sentence toward the body of the presentation → explicit bridge. SALIDA: numbered list with technique label, full opening text, and bridge sentence toward the development. CASOS BORDE: (a) skeptical or technical audience → avoid emotionalism; use statistic with source; (b) sensitive or crisis topic → omit micro-story; prefer reflective question; (c) virtual/webinar format → add pause instruction for engagement at the start. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: 3 openings, each between 130-200 words, distinct techniques, each ending with an explicit bridge. Trade-off: emotional impact vs. credibility → in technical audiences prioritize data over emotion. DoD: 3 complete variants, no technique placeholders unfilled, each autonomous. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the openings, state in one line the identified central tension.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_narrativa: [S · SITUATION] A sales, consulting, or product team needs to build the central section of a deck applying the Problem-Agitation-Solution (PAS) narrative structure: the problem is first stated, then the pain is intensified to create urgency, and finally the solution is presented as inevitable relief. [P · REQUEST] Draft the complete PAS narrative section for a deck, with the text of each slide (action headline + supporting copy + visual suggestion), organized in 3 blocks: P (Problem), A (Agitation), S (Solution). Deliverable: 6-9 structured slides with headline, copy, and visual suggestion per slide. [E · EXECUTION] ROL: Commercial narrative strategist and complex sales consultant with mastery of persuasive B2B frameworks. SUPUESTOS: if no number of slides is indicated, use 3 per block (9 total) [ASSUMPTION]; if no real quantitative data on the problem is available, mark [PENDING DATA] [ASSUMPTION]; if the audience is not specified, assume B2B economic decision-makers [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the problem description and proposed solution are missing (confidence < 0.85). INSUMOS: the user will paste the problem description, client/market context, solution offered, and available data. PASOS: 1. Define the problem in the client's terms (not the provider's) → problem headline. 2. Expand consequences of the unresolved problem with data or scenarios → 2-3 agitation slides. 3. Present the solution as a specific and measurable transformation → 2-3 solution slides. 4. For each slide: draft headline (action verb + consequence), supporting copy (2-3 bullets or 40 words), and visual suggestion (type of chart, image, or icon). 5. Verify that the P→A→S transition is emotionally and logically coherent. SALIDA: 9 slide cards with structure Block | No. | Headline | Copy | Suggested Visual. CASOS BORDE: (a) solution without a clear differentiator → focus on the process and guarantee, not the product; (b) audience already convinced of the problem → compress block P to 1 slide and expand S; (c) 5-minute presentation → reduce to 1 slide per block with minimal copy. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: 3 distinct blocks, each headline in active voice, no copy exceeds 50 words, visual suggestion in each slide. Trade-off: emotionality in agitation vs. credibility → balance with data when sharpening the pains. DoD: 9 complete cards, P→A→S flow clearly distinguishable, no invented data. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the cards, write in 2 lines the central dramatic tension of the narrative.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_cierre_ll: [S · SITUATION] A presenter is about to finish their deck and needs a close that consolidates the key message, eliminates uncertainty about the next step, and motivates the audience to act immediately or within a defined timeframe. A weak close wastes all the prior narrative work. [P · REQUEST] Draft the complete presentation close with: (1) 3-point value summary in ≤30 words, (2) single, concrete call to action with action verb + deadline + mechanism, (3) memorable closing phrase (insight, rhetorical question, or future projection). Deliverable: complete close text ready for the slide and for the speaker's voice. [E · EXECUTION] ROL: Persuasive communication strategist specializing in closings for sales presentations and leadership. SUPUESTOS: if no desired CTA is indicated, assume the objective is to schedule a follow-up meeting [ASSUMPTION]; if there is no explicit deadline, use 'within the next 5 business days' [ASSUMPTION]; if the audience is not specified, assume executives with decision-making power [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the main objective of the presentation is missing (confidence < 0.85). INSUMOS: the user will paste the 3 key points of the presentation, the desired CTA, audience, and context. PASOS: 1. Synthesize the 3 highest-value messages of the presentation → 3 bullets of ≤10 words each. 2. Build the CTA with formula: imperative verb + concrete benefit + deadline + mechanism → 1 action sentence. 3. Draft a memorable closing phrase that resonates with the opening or central problem → 1-2 sentences. 4. Integrate the 3 elements into flowing text for the slide (≤80 words) and into a speaker script (≤120 words). SALIDA: two versions of the close: (a) slide text ≤80 words and (b) speaker script ≤120 words with pause cues. CASOS BORDE: (a) audience with multiple stakeholders with different interests → differentiated CTA by role in speaker notes; (b) close of an internal alignment presentation → CTA is a team agreement, not a sale; (c) virtual presentation → add chat or poll instruction as the CTA mechanism. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: exactly 1 CTA with verb + deadline + mechanism, summary in ≤30 words, memorable closing phrase present. Trade-off: urgency vs. pressure → prioritize motivational urgency, avoid pressure that generates resistance. DoD: 2 versions delivered (slide + script), CTA without ambiguity, autonomous and memorable closing phrase. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the close, state in 1 line the dominant persuasive principle applied.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_guion_dia: [S · SITUATION] A presenter has the visual content of their deck ready (titles and bullets of each slide) but needs the speaker script (speaker notes) to know exactly what to say on each slide, how to transition to the next one, and how much time to spend. [P · REQUEST] Generate the complete speaker script, slide by slide, with: text to say (≤120 words per slide), transition sentence toward the next slide, and assigned time indication. Deliverable: structured document with Slide No. | Title | Script | Transition | Time (sec/min). [E · EXECUTION] ROL: Executive presentations coach with experience preparing speakers for conferences and C-level meetings. SUPUESTOS: if the number of slides is not provided, assume 10 slides [ASSUMPTION]; if no total duration is indicated, assume 20 minutes distributing time proportionally [ASSUMPTION]; if the tone is not specified, use conversational executive [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the slide content is not provided (confidence < 0.85). INSUMOS: the user will paste the content of each slide (title + bullets or existing text). PASOS: 1. Read and understand the content of all slides together → narrative flow map. 2. For each slide: expand bullets into fluid spoken prose (≤120 words) → speaker text. 3. Add transition sentence that logically connects to the next slide → 1 sentence. 4. Assign time in seconds or minutes based on the slide's weight within the total. 5. Identify 1-2 moments for a strategic pause or audience question → mark with [PAUSE] or [QUESTION]. SALIDA: table or structured list with No. | Title | Script (≤120 words) | Transition (1 sentence) | Time. CASOS BORDE: (a) dense slide with lots of data → condense to key insight + instruction to point at the visual; (b) agenda or index slide → script of 15-20 words maximum; (c) demo or video slide → introduction and closing script for the multimedia resource. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: script per slide ≤120 words, transition present on each slide, sum of times = agreed total duration. Trade-off: naturalness vs. completeness → prioritize short sentences and pauses over exhaustive explanations. DoD: complete script for all slides, no gaps, no generic non-contextualized presenter text. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the script, list in 3 bullets the oratory principles you will apply to this specific deck.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_una_idea_: [S · SITUATION] A presenter has a deck with overloaded slides: multiple ideas, long lists, or dense text on a single slide. They need to rewrite the content applying the "one idea per slide" principle to improve clarity, visual impact, and message retention. [P · REQUEST] Analyze the current deck content and restructure it so that each slide contains exactly one central idea expressed as: an action headline (≤12 words), supporting copy (≤30 words), and a visual or graphic suggestion. Deliverable: list of redesigned slides with the original vs. new slide count (may increase). [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Visual communication designer and content simplification specialist for executive presentations with experience in SlideDoc and McKinsey presentations. ASSUMPTIONS: if a slide has unrelated content, split it into as many slides as there are distinct ideas [ASSUMPTION]; if the total number of target slides is not specified, impose no limit—prioritize clarity [ASSUMPTION]; if the tone is not specified, use concise executive [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the current slide content is missing (confidence < 0.85). INPUTS: the user will paste the current content of each slide (existing title + text/bullets). STEPS: 1. Map distinct ideas on each original slide → concept count per slide. 2. Decide how to split or consolidate → restructuring plan (original N slides → new M slides). 3. For each new slide: write action headline ≤12 words + supporting copy ≤30 words + visual suggestion. 4. Verify that the narrative flow of the deck is maintained or improved after splitting. 5. Generate mapping table: Original slide | Ideas detected | New slides generated. OUTPUT: (a) restructuring mapping table and (b) complete cards for each new slide with No. | Headline | Copy | Suggested visual. EDGE CASES: (a) slide with a single well-expressed concept → keep it, indicate "no changes"; (b) deck with more than 20 slides → process in thematic blocks indicated by the user; (c) technical content with dependencies between concepts → maintain minimum context in the slide without violating the rule. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: no final slide has more than 1 central idea, headline ≤12 words, copy ≤30 words, visual suggestion on each slide. Trade-off: brevity vs. technical context → for technical content, 1 additional context sentence is permitted. DoD: complete mapping table + cards for all new slides, with no orphaned ideas. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the cards, show the original→new mapping table for validation.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_demo_prod: [S · SITUATION] A sales or presales team needs to deliver a live or recorded demonstration of a product or solution. The demo tends to focus on technical features rather than on benefits and client value, losing persuasive impact. [P · REQUEST] Write the complete script for a benefit-oriented product demo including: client-context introduction, sequence of demonstrated features linked to concrete benefits, audience validation moments, and a close with a next step. Deliverable: script by section with presenter text, on-screen actions, and explicit benefit. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior presales engineer and software demo consultant with experience in B2B consultative sales cycles for technology solutions. ASSUMPTIONS: if the audience profile is not specified, assume a technical-commercial decision-influencer [ASSUMPTION]; if the key features are not provided, the user will complete them in fields marked [PENDING FEATURE] [ASSUMPTION]; if the duration is not specified, assume a 20–30-minute demo [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the product name and client problem are missing (confidence < 0.85). INPUTS: the user will paste the product name, client's problem, features to demonstrate, and audience. STEPS: 1. Define the client scenario that justifies each feature → narrative context. 2. Structure the demo in acts: (a) scenario without the solution, (b) demonstration of the solution, (c) result with the solution. 3. For each feature: write presenter text (≤60 words) → on-screen action → explicit benefit (1 sentence). 4. Insert 2–3 validation moments ("does this solve the problem you mentioned?") → anchor questions. 5. Write the close with a summary of demonstrated benefits + concrete CTA. OUTPUT: table by section with columns: Act | Presenter text | On-screen action | Explicit benefit. EDGE CASES: (a) remote demo via video conference → add instructions for screen sharing and attention checkpoints; (b) advanced technical audience → go deeper on architecture in an optional appendix section; (c) demo without access to the real environment → adapt to a recorded demo with narration. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: each feature has an explicit benefit in 1 sentence, at least 2 validation questions are present, the close has 1 CTA with a concrete next step. Trade-off: technical completeness vs. time → prioritize the 3–5 highest-impact features over the full catalog. DoD: complete script by act, no features without an associated benefit, CTA present at the close. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the script, write in 1 sentence the "demo hero" (who benefits and how).
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_board_res: [S · SITUATION] A CEO, CFO, or area director needs to present the quarter's results to the board of directors. The audience has limited time, high rigor expectations, and expects both objective data and strategic context to guide decision-making. [P · REQUEST] Structure and write the complete quarterly results board presentation including: executive summary, key results vs. targets, analysis of significant variances, next-quarter outlook, and required decisions or approvals. Deliverable: slide structure with action headline, key data, and interpretive analysis per section. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: CFO and executive communication strategist with experience in quarterly presentations to boards of directors of mid- and large-scale companies. ASSUMPTIONS: if the actual results are not provided, the user will fill them in where indicated [PENDING DATA] [ASSUMPTION]; if the sector is not specified, assume a technology services company [ASSUMPTION]; if the number of slides is not specified, use the standard 8–10-slide board structure [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the quarter analyzed and whether results were positive, neutral, or negative are missing (confidence < 0.85). INPUTS: the user will paste results data, quarter targets, main KPIs, and available market context. STEPS: 1. Structure the results-vs.-targets section with a suggested table or chart and action headline → slides 2–3. 3. Analyze 2–3 significant variances (positive or negative) with root cause and action taken → slides 4–5. 4. Present the next-quarter outlook with hypotheses and commitments → slides 6–7. 5. OUTPUT: 8-slide structure with No. | Title | Action headline | Key content | Required data. EDGE CASES: (a) negative results → use a neutral descriptive headline before the diagnosis; (b) board with members lacking technical context → include a KPI glossary in the appendix; (c) 30-minute presentation → add market-context slides. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: each headline communicates a conclusion (not just a topic), the decisions section is separate and clear, data is marked [PENDING DATA] where missing. Trade-off: operational detail vs. strategic perspective → for a board, 80% strategic and 20% operational. DoD: 8 complete slides, decisions section present, no invented data. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the structure, write in 1 line the recommended narrative tone for the quarter (e.g., "solid management with warning signals").
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_storyline: [S · SITUATION] A consultant, analyst, or executive needs to structure the storyline of a complex presentation using the Minto Pyramid (Barbara Minto, SCQA + argumentation pyramid), which requires starting with the key conclusion or recommendation and supporting it with arguments grouped into logical blocks. [P · REQUEST] Build the complete presentation storyline using the Minto Pyramid with: situation, complication, implicit question, answer (recommendation), and a 2-level argument tree supporting the answer. Deliverable: text diagram of the pyramid + mapping of each node to a deck slide. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Strategic communication consultant and McKinsey analyst with command of the SCQA methodology and executive message structuring. ASSUMPTIONS: if the presentation type is not specified, assume a consulting proposal or strategic analysis [ASSUMPTION]; if the audience is not specified, assume executives with decision-making power and limited time [ASSUMPTION]; if there are more than 3 main arguments, the user will prioritize the strongest ones [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the central recommendation or the problem to solve is missing (confidence < 0.85). INPUTS: the user will paste the problem context, available data, audience, and tentative recommendation. STEPS: 1. Build the SCQA block: Situation (accepted context) → Complication (change or problem) → Implicit question (what should we do?) → Answer (main recommendation). 2. Develop the first pyramid level: 3 main arguments supporting the answer → grouped by type (deductive or inductive). 3. For each main argument, develop 2–3 pieces of evidence or second-level sub-arguments. 4. Map each pyramid node to a deck slide: SCQA → slides 1–2, arguments → slides 3–N, close → final slide. 5. Verify that the tree is MECE (mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive). OUTPUT: (a) text tree diagram of the Minto Pyramid and (b) mapping table Node | Slide | Suggested headline. EDGE CASES: (a) audience already knows the context → compress the situation to 1 sentence, expand arguments; (b) controversial recommendation → add an objection-anticipation block as a sub-level; (c) update presentation (not a proposal) → adapt SCQA to "situation update". [C · CRITERIA] Observable: pyramid with complete SCQA + minimum 3 level-1 arguments + minimum 2 pieces of evidence per argument, MECE verification indicated. Trade-off: exhaustiveness vs. clarity → prioritize 3 solid arguments over 5 weak ones. DoD: complete tree, mapping table with headlines, explicit MECE verification. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the pyramid, write in 1 line the central hypothesis of the presentation.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_manejo_ob: [S · SITUATION] A presenter knows their audience—whether investors, executives, clients, or committees—will arrive with predictable objections about price, viability, risk, or the competitive alternative. Instead of waiting for objections to arise in the Q&A, they want to incorporate them into the deck proactively and in a controlled manner. [P · REQUEST] Identify the 4–6 most likely objections for the presentation and write an anticipated-handling slide for each objection with: objection headline (in the voice of the client/audience), structured response (acknowledge + evidence + reframe), and suggested visual. Deliverable: 4–6 slide cards ready to insert into the deck or appendix. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Consultative sales and strategic negotiation consultant with experience in high-value decision-process objection handling. ASSUMPTIONS: if the most-feared objection types are not specified, infer them from the product/service and audience context [ASSUMPTION]; if it is not specified whether they go in the deck body or appendix, recommend the appendix to avoid interrupting the flow [ASSUMPTION]; if no supporting data is available, mark [PENDING EVIDENCE] [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the proposal description and audience are missing (confidence < 0.85). INPUTS: the user will paste the proposal description, audience, already-known objections, and available evidence. STEPS: 1. Infer or take the 4–6 most likely objections from context → list with objection type (price, risk, alternative, timing, etc.). 2. For each objection: write the objection in the client's first person (authentic voice) → 1 sentence. 3. Build the response in 3 parts: (a) acknowledge the concern (1 sentence), (b) present evidence or argument (2–3 bullets), (c) positive reframe (1 sentence). 4. Suggest a supporting visual (comparison table, ROI chart, testimonial, etc.) → 1 line. 5. Verify that no response sounds defensive or dismissive. OUTPUT: 4–6 cards with structure Objection | Acknowledgment | Evidence | Reframe | Suggested visual. EDGE CASES: (a) objection with no available evidence → acknowledge honestly and propose a validation plan; (b) emotional objection (distrust) → prioritize acknowledgment and testimonials over data; (c) critical objection that invalidates the proposal → reformulate the proposal before continuing. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: 4–6 cards, each response has 3 parts (acknowledge + evidence + reframe), no response exceeds 80 words, suggested visual on every card. Trade-off: honesty vs. persuasion → do not minimize valid objections; acknowledging real limitations strengthens credibility. DoD: 4–6 complete cards, no defensive responses, no invented evidence. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the cards, list the 4–6 identified objections for user validation.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_titulares: [S · SITUATION] A presenter has a deck with descriptive or thematic titles on each slide (e.g., "Sales Results", "Market Situation") that do not communicate the conclusion or move the audience to think or act. They need to convert them into action headlines that express the "so what" of each slide in a single active sentence. [P · REQUEST] Rewrite all the slide titles in the deck as action headlines: phrases containing subject + action or state verb + observable consequence, ≤15 words each. Deliverable: table with original title → action headline for each slide, plus a 1-line explanation of the change applied. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Executive communication editor and presentation-language specialist for senior-leadership audiences with strategic consulting experience. ASSUMPTIONS: if the slide content is not known (only its original title), infer the most likely headline and mark it [INFERRED] for the user to validate [ASSUMPTION]; if the presentation objective is not specified, assume the goal is to inform and persuade executives [ASSUMPTION]; if there are cover, index, or closing slides, write appropriate headlines for those formats [ASSUMPTION]; ask only if the list of original titles is not provided (confidence < 0.85). INPUTS: the user will paste the list of current slide titles and, optionally, the content of each one. STEPS: 1. Read all original titles and classify them: descriptive, thematic, interrogative, or already in action form. 2. For each title: identify the main conclusion or finding of that slide → "so what". 3. Write the action headline using the formula: subject + state/action verb + consequence → ≤15 words. 4. Add 1 line explaining the change applied (e.g., "from thematic to quantified conclusion"). 5. Verify that the set of headlines narrates a coherent story when read in sequence. OUTPUT: table with columns: No. | Original title | Action headline | Change applied | Narrative coherence (footnote if inconsistency exists). EDGE CASES: (a) title already in action form → keep it, indicate "kept"; (b) slide with no title → create a headline from scratch indicating [CREATED]; (c) very long deck (+20 slides) → process in thematic blocks. [C · CRITERIA] Observable: each headline ≤15 words, contains an action or state verb, the set narrates coherently when read in sequence. Trade-off: impact vs. precision → if the headline becomes too cryptic to be precise, allow up to 18 words with a note. DoD: all original titles converted, complete table, narrative coherence verified. Protocolo MetodologIA: before the table, write in 1 sentence the master message the headlines should narrate in sequence.
spec-comunicacion_presentacion_webinar_e: [S · SITUATION] A B2B marketing team needs to design the complete structure of a 60-minute webinar oriented toward generating qualified demand for a product or service. The webinar must capture the attendee's attention, deliver real value, and lead to a concrete commercial action at the end. [P · REQUEST] Produce a webinar structure outline with timed sections, objective for each block, transition scripts, engagement mechanisms, and a final call to action, ready to be developed by the content team. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior B2B content marketing strategist with experience designing high-impact, high-conversion virtual events. ASSUMPTIONS: total duration 60 minutes [ASSUMPTION], mid-to-senior decision-maker audience [ASSUMPTION], product or service with a consultative sales cycle [ASSUMPTION]; if the actual context differs, the user must indicate it. INPUTS: paste the product or service name, the central problem it solves, and the target attendee profile. STEPS: 1. Define the opening hook (first 3 minutes): webinar headline, value promise, and presenter credential. 2. Structure the educational block (minutes 4–35): 3–4 high-value content blocks with scripted transitions. 3. Design engagement moments (polls, questions, brief exercises) distributed every 10–12 minutes. 4. Create the transition to the offer (minutes 36–45): success story or demonstration that connects the content to the solution. 5. Articulate the call to action (minutes 46–55): specific offer, genuine urgency, and response mechanism. 6. Close with a Q&A session (last 5 minutes): closing script and CTA reminder. OUTPUT: structured document with a time table, objective per block, suggested transition text, and production checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) if the webinar is 30 minutes, compress educational blocks to 2 and remove Q&A; (b) if the product requires a technical demonstration, insert a live demo block with a recorded backup; (c) if the audience is purely technical, replace the success story with verifiable data and metrics. [C · CRITERIA] Each block has a measurable objective (retention, survey clicks, attendees who reach the CTA); the education-to-offer transition does not create a bait-and-switch feeling; the CTA is actionable in under 2 minutes; the outline can be executed without modification by a presenter who did not participate in its design. Trade-off: content depth vs. time available for the CTA; prioritize value density in the first 35 minutes. DoD: outline with all blocks complete, times assigned, and at least 3 engagement moments documented. Protocolo MetodologIA: first structure the attendee's transformation, then build the offer as a natural consequence of the value delivered.
spec-comunicacion_copy_titular_4u: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team needs high-impact headlines for advertising campaigns. Current headlines are generic and fail to stop the scroll or motivate the click. The 4U formula (Urgent, Unique, Ultra-Specific, Useful) is the proven framework for producing headlines that convert. [P · REQUEST] Generate a set of 8 advertising headlines applying the complete 4U formula, for the indicated product or service, ready to be tested in digital or print campaigns. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior direct-response copywriter with over 10 years writing headlines for Spanish-speaking markets. ASSUMPTIONS: main channel is digital (social or search) [ASSUMPTION], adult audience with purchasing power [ASSUMPTION], product or service with a differentiating value proposition [ASSUMPTION]; declare if context differs. INPUTS: paste the product or service name, the main value proposition, and the target audience segment. STEPS: 1. Identify the central tension or desire of the target segment from the input received. 2. Generate 2 headlines maximizing URGENCY (deadline, scarcity, consequence of not acting). 3. Generate 2 headlines maximizing UNIQUENESS (exclusive differentiator, angle not exploited by competitors). 4. Generate 2 headlines maximizing ULTRA-SPECIFICITY (number, data point, concrete result). 5. Generate 2 headlines maximizing UTILITY (clear and immediate functional benefit). 6. For each headline, note which 4U dimension dominates and the emotional hook it activates. OUTPUT: table with 8 headlines, dominant 4U dimension, emotional hook, and character length. EDGE CASES: (a) if the product is regulated (health, finance), avoid unverifiable superlatives and annotate [ASSUMPTION] on figures; (b) if headlines are needed for email, limit to 50 characters; (c) if the brand has tone restrictions, apply a brand-voice filter before delivering. [C · CRITERIA] Each headline scores above 3 of the 4U dimensions; none repeat the same emotional hook; all are actionable without additional context; the table can be used directly in a creative brief sheet. Trade-off: specificity vs. reach; prioritize headlines with concrete data even if they reduce the potential audience. DoD: 8 headlines in a complete table with the 3 required columns. Protocolo MetodologIA: write the headline that would convert best first, then the rest in descending order of estimated impact.
spec-comunicacion_copy_landing_pas: [S · SITUATION] A company launches or renews a conversion landing page for a product or service. The current copy does not emotionally connect with the visitor or naturally lead them toward action. The PAS framework (Problem-Agitation-Solution) is the most effective persuasion structure for landing pages because it follows the emotional journey of the prospect. [P · REQUEST] Write the complete landing page copy structured with the PAS framework: problem section, agitation section, solution section, value proposition, benefit bullets, social proof, and call to action; all ready to be laid out. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Conversion copywriter specialized in B2B and B2C landing pages for Spanish-speaking markets. ASSUMPTIONS: the landing page has a single conversion objective [ASSUMPTION], the visitor arrives cold or warm from an ad or organic search [ASSUMPTION], the product has at least one success story or testimonial available [ASSUMPTION]; the user must adjust any assumptions that do not apply. INPUTS: paste the product or service name, the problem it solves, the ideal client, and any available testimonials or result data. STEPS: 1. Write the main headline and subheadline that captures attention in 3 seconds. 2. Develop the PROBLEM block: describe the pain in the client's language, 60–80 words. 3. Develop the AGITATION block: amplify the emotional and economic consequences if the problem is not resolved, 80–100 words. 4. Develop the SOLUTION block: present the product as the inevitable answer, 80–100 words. 5. Write 5 benefit bullets in feature-advantage-benefit format. 6. Write 1–2 testimonials in a validated structure (if none are available, mark with [ASSUMPTION]). 7. Write the main call to action with supporting microcopy. OUTPUT: complete copy by sections with block labels (Headline, Problem, Agitation, Solution, Benefits, Social Proof, CTA), word count per section, and minimal design notes. EDGE CASES: (a) if the product is technical, add a "how it works" section of 3 steps between Solution and Benefits; (b) if the objective is lead capture rather than direct sale, adapt the CTA to a registration form; (c) if the audience is skeptical, add an answered-objections block. [C · CRITERIA] The visitor recognizes their problem in the first 50 words; the agitation-to-solution transition is fluid and not forced; each bullet has a measurable or perceptible benefit; the CTA uses a first-person action verb. Trade-off: length vs. reading rate; prioritize scannable copy with implicit visual hierarchy. DoD: all PAS sections complete with word count and at least 5 benefit bullets. Protocolo MetodologIA: write from the internal voice of the ideal prospect; the copy must sound as if the visitor were describing themselves before discovering the solution.
spec-comunicacion_copy_propuesta_valor: [S · SITUATION] A company or professional needs to articulate their value proposition clearly and precisely in a single sentence that simultaneously answers: who is it for?, what does it do?, how is it different?, and what concrete result does it produce? Current statements are vague, too long, or company-centric rather than client-centric. [P · REQUEST] Produce 5 versions of the value proposition in a single sentence, following different proven templates, select the strongest one and explain why, ready for use on a homepage, pitch, and sales materials. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Strategic positioning consultant with experience in startups, mid-sized companies, and B2B personal brands. ASSUMPTIONS: the product or service already exists and has at least one documented client or use case [ASSUMPTION], the target audience is defined even if broadly [ASSUMPTION]; the user must adjust if this is not the case. INPUTS: paste the business or product name, the description of what it does, the target client, and the main result it generates (with figures if available). STEPS: 1. Extract from the input: who the client is, what problem they have, what the product does, what result it delivers, and what differentiates it. 2. Write 5 versions using these templates: (a) We help [who] achieve [result] without [usual friction]; (b) The [category] platform/service that [differentiator] for [who]; (c) [Transformation verb] for [who] who wants [result] but has [obstacle]; (d) [Measurable result] for [who] using [differentiating mechanism]; (e) free version combining the best elements. 3. Evaluate each version on: clarity (0–3), specificity (0–3), desire generated (0–3). 4. Select the winner and justify the choice with explicit criteria. OUTPUT: table with 5 versions, score on the 3 dimensions, justified selection, and usage note (where to place each version if only one is not chosen). EDGE CASES: (a) if the business has multiple segments, produce one version per priority segment; (b) if the differentiator is not clear, flag it explicitly and propose 2 differentiator hypotheses; (c) if the value proposition involves a key figure (ROI, time), mark with [ASSUMPTION] if not validated. [C · CRITERIA] Each sentence is under 20 words; the client can read it and say "that is exactly what I need" without additional context; it uses no internal jargon or empty adjectives ("innovative", "leader", "world-class"). Trade-off: specificity vs. universality; prioritize specificity even if it reduces perceived reach. DoD: 5 versions in a table with scores and justified selection. Protocolo MetodologIA: the best value proposition speaks the client's language, not the company's.
spec-comunicacion_copy_bullets_beneficio: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team needs to replace lists of technical features that do not connect with the buyer with benefit bullets that activate the desire to purchase. The feature-advantage-benefit (FAB) translation method transforms functional attributes into emotional and practical reasons to buy. [P · REQUEST] Take the provided list of product or service features and produce 8 complete benefit bullets using the FAB chain, ordered from highest to lowest persuasive impact. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Sales copywriter specializing in product copy for e-commerce, SaaS, and professional services in Spanish. ASSUMPTIONS: the provided features are real and verifiable [ASSUMPTION], the customer buys primarily motivated by saving time, money, or effort [ASSUMPTION]; adjust if the main motivation is different. INPUTS: paste the product feature list (minimum 6, maximum 15) and the target buyer profile. STEPS: 1. For each received feature identify: what it does (feature), what it improves for the user (advantage), what the user achieves or avoids in terms of life or business (benefit). 2. Write the complete bullet in the format: [Main benefit in bold or uppercase] — [advantage] thanks to [technical feature]. 3. Add an emotional trigger at the end of each bullet (saves, eliminates, guarantees, doubles, etc.). 4. Order the 8 bullets from highest to lowest estimated impact according to the purchase motivation of the indicated profile. 5. Add a brief note explaining the ordering criterion. OUTPUT: list of 8 formatted bullets with the explicit FAB structure in a side column and ordering note. EDGE CASES: (a) if the product has technical features that are hard to translate, add a daily-use analogy; (b) if there are known negative features or limitations, transform them into honesty that builds trust; (c) if the buyer profile is technical, keep technical language in the feature but humanize the benefit. [C · CRITERIA] Each bullet has the three identifiable FAB elements; the benefit is concrete and not generic ("improves your life" is not valid); the emotional trigger is different in each bullet; the complete list can be copied directly to a product sheet. Trade-off: bullet length vs. scannability; maximum 25 words per bullet. DoD: 8 bullets with explicit FAB structure, ordered and with an ordering criterion note. Protocolo MetodologIA: the buyer does not buy features, they buy the improved version of themselves; write from that future.
spec-comunicacion_copy_cta_variantes: [S · SITUATION] A marketing or design team needs to test different versions of the call to action (CTA) on a page, email, or ad to identify which one generates the highest click and conversion rate. The variants must differ in their psychological angle, not just in wording. [P · REQUEST] Generate 8 CTA variants for the indicated context, organized into 4 A/B test pairs with contrasting psychological angles, with a hypothesis for why each variant might win and optional support microcopy. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Conversion rate optimization (CRO) specialist with experience in A/B testing for websites, emails, and ads in Spanish-speaking markets. ASSUMPTIONS: the target action is defined (click, registration, purchase) [ASSUMPTION], the context is digital [ASSUMPTION], the audience has sufficient volume for statistically significant tests [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: paste the target action (what you want the user to do), the context where the CTA will appear (page, email, banner), and the audience profile. STEPS: 1. Define the target action and the user's mental state just before seeing the CTA. 2. Generate 4 pairs of variants, each pair contrasting a psychological axis: (a) Benefit vs. Urgency; (b) Action Verb vs. Result Verb; (c) Personalization ("my"/"your") vs. Collective; (d) Direct vs. Low Commitment ("no credit card", "free for 14 days"). 3. For each variant: button text (maximum 6 words), optional support microcopy (1 line), hypothesis for why it might win. 4. Indicate the contrasted psychological axis in each pair. OUTPUT: table of 4 pairs with variant A, variant B, psychological axis, support microcopy, and winner hypothesis. EDGE CASES: (a) if the context is email, adapt the CTA to text link and button style; (b) if the action has high friction (immediate payment), always add a low-commitment variant; (c) if the product is regulated, avoid unprovable absolute guarantees. [C · CRITERIA] Each CTA has fewer than 6 words; the 4 pairs contrast different psychological axes; the hypotheses are falsifiable with real metrics; the table is ready to load into an A/B testing tool. Trade-off: creativity vs. clarity; prioritize unambiguous clarity of action. DoD: 4 complete pairs with all fields and hypotheses per variant. Protocolo MetodologIA: the best CTA makes the user feel they are making the decision themselves, not that they are being pushed.
spec-comunicacion_copy_email_marketing_s: [S · SITUATION] A company or entrepreneur is launching a new product, service, or program and needs a complete launch email sequence that warms up the audience, generates anticipation, presents the offer, and closes with real urgency. The sequence must function as a system of progressive persuasion, not as a series of disconnected emails. [P · REQUEST] Write a 5-email launch sequence (pre-sale, opening, value, urgency, and close) with subject line, preview text, complete body, and call to action for each email, ready to load into any email marketing platform. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Email marketing strategist specializing in digital product and service launches for Spanish-speaking markets. ASSUMPTIONS: the list has subscribers who know the sender but do not know the product being launched [ASSUMPTION], the launch has a sales period of 5-7 days [ASSUMPTION], there is a special launch offer (price or bonus) [ASSUMPTION]; the user should adjust if this does not apply. INPUTS: paste the name of the product or service, the value proposition, the price or launch offer, the audience, and any deadline. STEPS: 1. Email 1 - Pre-sale (D-3): awaken curiosity without revealing the product, personal narrative hook. 2. Email 2 - Opening (D-0): launch announcement, complete value proposition, CTA to cart or sales page. 3. Email 3 - Value (D+1): deliver related educational content that reinforces the need for the product. 4. Email 4 - Urgency (D+3): reminder with social proof (real testimonials or [ASSUMPTION]), scarcity or real deadline. 5. Email 5 - Close (D+5, last day): maximum urgency, empathetic close, last opportunity. For each email: subject line (max. 50 characters), preview text (max. 100 characters), body (150-300 words), specific CTA. OUTPUT: 5 complete emails with field labels (Subject, Preview, Body, CTA), body word count, and personalization notes. EDGE CASES: (a) if the launch has limited access (spots), use real scarcity of spots; (b) if the list is cold or disengaged, add a re-engagement email 0 five days before; (c) if there is no price offer, use an exclusive launch bonus. [C · CRITERIA] Each subject line has different hooks (curiosity, benefit, urgency, social proof, scarcity); the body of each email has a single central idea; the emotional progression goes from curiosity to desire to action; the CTAs differ in text but are consistent in destination. Trade-off: email length vs. open rate; body between 150-300 words to maintain mobile readability. DoD: 5 complete emails with all fields, word count, and personalization notes. Protocolo MetodologIA: a launch sequence does not sell a product, it sells the transformation; each email brings the reader one step closer to believing the transformation is possible for them.
spec-comunicacion_copy_descripcion_produ: [S · SITUATION] An e-commerce, marketplace, or digital catalog business needs product descriptions that go beyond listing technical specifications and that activate the desire to purchase by connecting features with emotional and functional benefits. The current descriptions are flat, SEO-mechanical, or copied from the manufacturer. [P · REQUEST] Write the complete conversion-oriented product description: emotional opening paragraph, FAB benefit bullets, humanized technical specifications, and call to action, ready to publish on the product sheet. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: E-commerce copywriter specializing in product sheet copy for Spanish-language stores with experience in physical and digital categories. ASSUMPTIONS: the product is real and its specifications are verifiable [ASSUMPTION], the buyer arrived at the sheet with medium-to-high purchase intent [ASSUMPTION], the platform allows between 150 and 400 words in the description [ASSUMPTION]; the user adjusts if the limit is different. INPUTS: paste the product name, its technical specifications or main features, the target buyer profile, and the price or price range. STEPS: 1. Write an opening paragraph of 40-60 words that places the buyer in the moment of use or benefit of the product (use scene). 2. Develop 5 FAB (Feature-Advantage-Benefit) bullets of maximum 20 words each. 3. Present technical specifications in a humanized table format (attribute name in the buyer's language, not the manufacturer's). 4. Add an "ideal for" section with 3 concrete use cases. 5. Close with a CTA sentence that reinforces the decision. OUTPUT: complete description with 5 labeled sections, total word count, and 80-word short version for product card or list view. EDGE CASES: (a) if the product is a specialized technical product, maintain terminology but add a daily analogy; (b) if the product has certifications or warranties, mention them in the specifications section as trust triggers; (c) if the price is premium, open with the aspirational, not with functionality. [C · CRITERIA] The opening paragraph does not mention the product name in the first sentence; each bullet has the three FAB elements; the complete description is between 150 and 350 words; the short version works independently. Trade-off: information density vs. reading flow; prioritize flow. DoD: complete description with all sections, word count, and 80-word short version. Protocolo MetodologIA: the buyer does not read the product description, they use it to confirm a decision they almost already made; write to reinforce that certainty.
spec-comunicacion_copy_microcopy_ux: [S · SITUATION] A product or design team needs microcopy for the most critical friction points in a digital interface: empty states, error messages, tooltips, placeholders, confirmations, and onboarding. The current microcopy is generic, technical, or nonexistent, which increases the abandonment rate and reduces user satisfaction. [P · REQUEST] Write action-oriented microcopy for the 8 most common state types in digital interfaces, calibrated for the brand voice and user flow context, ready to be delivered to the development team. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: UX writer specializing in microcopy and interface writing for digital products in Spanish. ASSUMPTIONS: the interface is a web or mobile application [ASSUMPTION], the brand has a tone between close and professional [ASSUMPTION], the user is an adult with basic app experience [ASSUMPTION]; adjust if the context differs. INPUTS: paste the product or app name, description of the main function, brand tone (formal/close/playful), and the list of interface elements that need microcopy. STEPS: 1. Define the brand voice in 3 adjectives from the input. 2. For each received interface element, write: version A (user action-oriented) and version B (action benefit-oriented). 3. Include the 8 standard types if not in the input: empty state, validation error, system error, field placeholder, tooltip, confirmation message, limit reached notice, and onboarding CTA. 4. For each piece of microcopy: maximum 1-2 sentences, no technical jargon, with an action verb in the imperative or first person. 5. Flag if any piece needs to coordinate with the legal team (personal data, terms). OUTPUT: table with state type, version A, version B, character length, and coordination note where applicable. EDGE CASES: (a) if the tone is very formal (banking, health), remove colloquialisms and use formal address; (b) if the error is from the system and not the user, never blame the user in the message; (c) if the empty state is first-time use, guide toward the initial action, do not describe the absence of data. [C · CRITERIA] Each piece has fewer than 120 characters; none uses the word "error" alone without actionable context; empty states have an implicit or explicit CTA; the tone is consistent with the 3 brand voice adjectives. Trade-off: brevity vs. context; prioritize brevity and add tooltip for additional context if necessary. DoD: 8 state types with version A and B, characters counted, and coordination notes. Protocolo MetodologIA: microcopy does not describe what happened, it guides the user toward what to do next.
spec-comunicacion_copy_anuncio_google_se: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team or agency needs to write responsive search ads (RSA) for Google Ads in Spanish, strictly respecting the platform's character limits: headlines of maximum 30 characters (15 headlines) and descriptions of maximum 90 characters (4 descriptions). The current ads are generic, do not include the main keyword, and do not respond to the searcher's intent. [P · REQUEST] Write a complete set of 15 headlines and 4 descriptions for a responsive search ad, aligned with the indicated search intent, within Google Ads' exact limits, ready to load into the platform. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Google Ads specialist with experience in copy for search campaigns in Spanish-speaking markets, focused on CTR and quality relevance. [ASSUMPTION]: The final URL already exists and the offer is real. ASSUMPTIONS: the ad is for a standard search campaign [ASSUMPTION], the audience uses Google on desktop or mobile [ASSUMPTION], the goal is clicks to a conversion landing page [ASSUMPTION]. INPUTS: paste the name of the product or service, the main keyword, the differentiating benefit, the main CTA, and the destination URL. STEPS: 1. Identify the search intent (informational, navigational, commercial, transactional) from the keyword. 2. Write 15 headlines of maximum 30 characters each, distributed across 3 groups: 5 with the keyword or variant, 5 with benefit or differentiator, 5 with CTA or urgency. 3. Write 4 descriptions of maximum 90 characters each: 2 focused on benefit and 2 on action/urgency. 4. Verify the character count of each piece (count includes spaces). 5. Add a note on which headlines to pin in position 1, 2, or 3 for maximum relevance. OUTPUT: table of 15 headlines with character count, table of 4 descriptions with character count, pinning note, and Google Ads policy compliance checklist. EDGE CASES: (a) if the keyword has more than 30 characters, use dynamic keyword insertion {KeyWord:Alternative}; (b) if the business is regulated (health, finance, lawyers), remove superlatives and mention relevant legal restrictions; (c) if the goal is a phone call, add at least 2 headlines with a number or call CTA. [C · CRITERIA] All headlines are within the exact 30 characters; all descriptions within the exact 90 characters; the 15 headlines cover the 3 groups without repeating the same benefit; the policy checklist has no failed items. Trade-off: keyword inclusion vs. text flow; prioritize quality relevance. DoD: 15 headlines and 4 descriptions with verified character count, pinning note, and policy checklist. Protocolo MetodologIA: each headline is a direct response to what the searcher has in mind at that precise moment.
spec-comunicacion_copy_anuncio_social_pa: [S · SITUATION] A marketing team needs to write copy for paid social media ads (Meta, TikTok, LinkedIn, or Instagram) that stop the scroll, emotionally connect with the audience, and drive the target action. The current ads are too corporate or not adapted to each platform's format. [P · REQUEST] Write 3 complete copy variants for paid ads on the indicated platform: main text, ad headline, and description, each with a distinct creative angle, ready to upload to the platform along with the recommended visual reference. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Media buyer and creative copywriter specializing in paid social campaigns for Spanish-speaking markets. ASSUMPTIONS: the audience does not know the brand (cold or look-alike audience) [ASSUMPTION], the budget allows testing 3 variants [ASSUMPTION], the goal is conversion or lead capture [ASSUMPTION]; the user adjusts if this does not apply. INPUTS: paste the product or service, the target audience, the campaign objective (conversion, traffic, leads), the platform, and the brand tone. STEPS: 1. Define 3 distinct creative angles: (a) customer pain/problem; (b) transformation/result; (c) social proof or curiosity. 2. For each angle write: main text (max. 150 words), ad headline (max. 40 characters), link description (max. 30 characters). 3. For each variant add: recommended visual format description (static image, video, carousel), script for the first 3 seconds of video if applicable. 4. Indicate which variant to test first and why. OUTPUT: 3 complete variants with field labels, word/character count, recommended visual description, and testing priority note. EDGE CASES: (a) if the platform is LinkedIn, use a more formal tone and focus on ROI and productivity; (b) if it is TikTok, the main text copy can be more casual and the first 3 seconds of the script are critical; (c) if the audience is very segmented (retargeting), use the social proof variant first. [C · CRITERIA] Each variant's main text opens with a hook that does not start with the brand name; the ad headline has a clear benefit or question; the 3 variants use distinct creative angles without repeating the same emotional hook; the copy is adapted to the language of the indicated platform. Trade-off: creativity vs. offer clarity; prioritize offer clarity. DoD: 3 complete variants with all fields, count, recommended visual, and priority note. Protocolo MetodologIA: in paid social, copy's first job is to stop the scroll; the second is to make the user forget they are watching an ad.
spec-comunicacion_copy_pagina_ventas_lar: [S · SITUATION] A digital business, coach, consultant, or service company needs a long-form sales page for a mid-to-high-priced product that requires building trust, answering objections, and driving purchase in a single visit. The current page is short, does not address the buyer's objections, or lacks the persuasive structure necessary for the product's price. [P · REQUEST] Write the complete copy for a long-form sales page with all structural blocks: headline, problem, credibility story, value proposition, program or product content, benefits, social proof, who it is for, who it is not for, common objections, guarantee, price, and final CTA, ready to be laid out. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Direct-response copywriter specializing in high-conversion long-form sales pages for Spanish-speaking markets, with experience in education, coaching, consulting, and software products. ASSUMPTIONS: the product price is between 200 and 2,000 USD or equivalent [ASSUMPTION], the visitor arrives with prior knowledge of the problem but without having seen the solution [ASSUMPTION], at least one client testimonial or result exists [ASSUMPTION]; the user adjusts what does not apply. INPUTS: paste the name of the product or program, the value proposition, the price, the modules or deliverables, available testimonials, the guarantee if it exists, and the ideal buyer profile. STEPS: 1. Write the main headline + subtitle that captures the problem and promises the transformation in 2 sentences. 2. Problem block: identify the pain using the customer's own language (100-150 words). 3. Author or company credibility story: why they are the authoritative source (80-120 words). 4. Value proposition: the specific transformation the product produces (60-80 words). 5. Program content: list of modules, deliverables, or main features with a benefit per item. 6. Benefits section: 6 high-impact FAB bullets. 7. Social proof: 2-3 structured testimonials (result + name + context); if none are real, mark with [ASSUMPTION]. 8. Who it is for: 5 items of ideal buyer profile. 9. Who it is not for: 3 items of active disqualification (builds trust). 10. Response to 4 common objections in question-and-answer format. 11. Guarantee: write the guarantee in a way that eliminates perceived risk. 12. Price and final CTA: price presentation with anchoring and immediate-action CTA. OUTPUT: complete copy with 12 labeled sections, word count per section and total, and minimal design note per block. EDGE CASES: (a) if the product is technical (SaaS, tool), add a guided demo or screenshot section; (b) if the price is very high (+5,000 USD), remove the price from the page and redirect to a discovery call; (c) if there is no guarantee, offer a review session or trial access as a substitute. [C · CRITERIA] The complete page is between 1,500 and 3,000 words; the problem block uses exactly the language the buyer would use to describe it; the objections address the 4 most common purchase barriers (price, time, doubts that it works, doubts that it works for me); the CTA uses a first-person verb. Trade-off: length vs. bounce rate; prioritize emotional progression that justifies the length. DoD: 12 complete sections with labels, word count, and design note. Protocolo MetodologIA: a long-form sales page does not convince the buyer, it gives them permission to make a decision they already wanted to make; write to remove the obstacles, not to create the desire.
spec-comunicacion_copy_prueba_social: [S · SITUATION] A company or professional needs to build credibility on a sales page, commercial proposal, or landing page, and has real client testimonials, reviews, or metrics. The goal is to convert that evidence into a social proof block that eliminates prospect resistance. [P · REQUEST] A publish-ready social proof block that includes: (1) 3-5 testimonials formatted with a highlighted quote + name + role/company + quantifiable result, (2) a logos or mentions section if applicable, (3) a key satisfaction or usage statistic, and (4) a 2-line closing micro-argument that reinforces trust. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior conversion copywriter with experience in CRO (conversion rate optimization) and B2B/B2C persuasive copywriting. ASSUMPTIONS: if no real testimonials are provided, example testimonials marked as [EXAMPLE — replace with real data] are created; the tone is professional-warm unless otherwise indicated; the format is HTML/plain text at the user's choice; if sector confidence is below 0.85, ask for sector and target client before proceeding. INPUTS: testimonials, reviews, metrics, or screenshots pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Analyze the received testimonials and identify the 3-5 most impactful ones with a measurable result → prioritized list with justification. 2. Reformat each testimonial in a quote-name-role-result structure → clean block. 3. Write a key 1-line statistic if satisfaction/NPS/usage data are provided → figure + source or [ASSUMPTION]. 4. Write a 2-line closing micro-argument → text. 5. Assemble the complete block in copy-ready format → final artifact. OUTPUT: Document with sections: «Formatted Testimonials», «Key Statistic», «Trust Micro-Close»; consistent tone; length: 300-500 words. EDGE CASES: (a) Only one testimonial is available → expand with industry statistics marked [INDUSTRY DATA] and request more testimonials; (b) The testimonials have no quantifiable results → rewrite focusing on qualitative transformation and flag it; (c) Regulated sector (health, finance) → add a suggested disclaimer. [C · CRITERIA] Each testimonial includes at least one concrete result (figure, percentage, or observable change). The statistic has a source or marker. The block can be copied directly without structural editing. Trade-off: authenticity > literary creativity. DoD: block reviewed, formatted, and ready to insert into the page without additional modifications. Protocolo MetodologIA: evidence before publishing — label each piece of data as [CODE], [REAL DATA], or [ASSUMPTION].
spec-comunicacion_copy_garantia_reduccio: [S · SITUATION] A business selling a product or service faces cart abandonment or rejection at the decision stage because prospects perceive risk in the purchase (losing money, not obtaining the promised result, complications). The company wants to write a guarantee declaration that neutralizes that resistance in a credible and specific way. [P · REQUEST] A guarantee declaration ready to include on a sales page, proposal, or closing email that contains: (1) the guarantee name (memorable, not generic), (2) clear and simple activation conditions, (3) a concrete promise of what is returned or resolved, and (4) a 2-3 line narrative paragraph that humanizes the guarantee and builds trust. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Conversion copywriting specialist with experience in reducing friction at closing stages and structuring high-impact guarantees. ASSUMPTIONS: if the type of possible guarantee is not indicated (refund, retry, result guarantee), three variants are proposed for the user to choose; the default period is 30 days unless otherwise indicated; neutral-professional brand language is assumed; if confidence in the sector's legal conditions is below 0.85, confirmation is requested before proceeding and a disclaimer is added. INPUTS: description of the product/service and any existing return policy pasted in the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the main type of risk perceived by the buyer (economic, time, result) → one-line diagnosis. 2. Define the guarantee name that reflects the central promise → 2-3 name options. 3. Write the activation conditions in simple language (max. 3 bullets) → draft. 4. Write the concrete resolution promise → one direct sentence. 5. Write the 2-3 line humanizing narrative paragraph → draft. 6. Assemble the complete declaration → final artifact. OUTPUT: Section «Guarantee [Name]» with name, conditions, promise, and narrative paragraph; total 80-150 words; confident and empathetic tone. EDGE CASES: (a) Digital product with no real refund option → redirect toward support guarantee or free retry; (b) Regulated sector that prohibits result promises → reformulate as «process commitment» with disclaimer; (c) Company with high refund history → simplify conditions and omit lengthy restrictions to avoid planting doubt. [C · CRITERIA] The declaration neutralizes the buyer's most frequent fear. The conditions are so clear they do not generate support questions. The narrative paragraph has a human voice, not a corporate one. Trade-off: simplicity > legal exhaustiveness. DoD: declaration reviewed, with name, conditions, promise, and narrative, ready to insert. Protocolo MetodologIA: declare each policy assumption with [ASSUMPTION] for the client's legal validation.
spec-comunicacion_copy_titular_swipe: [S · SITUATION] A copywriter, marketer, or content creator needs to generate multiple persuasive headline variants for a product, service, article, or campaign. They require speed, a variety of angles, and adherence to formulas with a proven conversion track record (curiosity gap, direct benefit, urgency, fear of missing out, number, question, etc.). [P · REQUEST] A bank of 20 ready-to-use headlines organized into 5 proven-formula categories (4 headlines per category), applied to the specific topic provided, with a usage note for each category. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior direct-response copywriter with more than 10 years applying swipe files and headline frameworks in email, ad, and landing page campaigns. ASSUMPTIONS: the topic or product is inferred from the thread; if no target audience is specified, a professional adult Spanish-speaking audience is assumed; the default tone is active and direct; the 5 formula categories are: (1) Curiosity/Intrigue, (2) Direct benefit + number, (3) Urgency/Scarcity, (4) Problem-solution, (5) Provocative question; if confidence in the topic is below 0.85, ask for the main benefit before proceeding. INPUTS: description of the product, service, article, or campaign pasted into the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the core benefit, main pain point, and differentiating promise → 3-line synthesis. 2. Generate 4 headlines for the Curiosity/Intrigue category → list. 3. Generate 4 headlines for the Direct benefit + number category → list. 4. Generate 4 headlines for the Urgency/Scarcity category → list. 5. Generate 4 headlines for the Problem-solution category → list. 6. Generate 4 headlines for the Provocative question category → list. 7. Add a 1-line usage note per category → final bank. OUTPUT: "Bank of 20 headlines" document with 5 categorized sections, usage note per section, and summary table of the 3 most recommended headlines with justification. EDGE CASES: (a) Very technical or niche topic → simplify language in curiosity and problem-solution headlines and note it; (b) Sensitive sector (health, finance, legal) → avoid absolute promises and add a compliance note; (c) Headlines for SEO → add a natural-keyword variant in each category. [C · CRITERIA] Each headline is fewer than 12 words. At least 15 of 20 include an action verb or number. The bank can be used directly in A/B testing without additional review. Trade-off: variety > unit perfection. DoD: 20 headlines written, categorized, with usage notes and a recommended table. Protocolo MetodologIA: flag with [ADAPTAR] headlines that require additional personalization before launch.
spec-comunicacion_story_viaje_heroe: [S · SITUATION] A brand, company, or professional wants to build its central communication narrative using Joseph Campbell's hero's journey archetype, adapted to the commercial context. They need a story that positions the customer as the hero, the brand as the mentor, and the product or service as the "elixir" that transforms the hero's situation. [P · REQUEST] A complete brand narrative in the "hero's journey" format adapted to 7 commercial stages, ready to use in a pitch, about page, presentation, or brand video, with a long version (500-700 words) and a short version (100-150 words). [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Brand strategist and storyteller with experience in transformation narratives for B2B and B2C communication. ASSUMPTIONS: the hero is the brand's ideal customer; the brand fulfills the role of mentor/guide, not the hero; if the ideal customer is not specified, it is inferred from the sector and the described offering; the 7 stages are: (1) Customer's ordinary world, (2) Call to adventure / problem, (3) Resistance / fears, (4) The mentor / brand appears, (5) Trial and transformation, (6) Concrete result / new reality, (7) Call to others / social proof; if confidence is below 0.85 on the ideal customer profile, ask before drafting. INPUTS: description of the company, its product/service, and its ideal customer pasted into the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the customer's "ordinary world" (starting situation, pains, context) → opening paragraph. 2. Articulate the problem or "call" that destabilizes that world → 1-2 sentences. 3. Describe the resistance and fears that hold back action → 2-3 lines. 4. Introduce the brand as an empathetic and authoritative mentor → 2-3 lines. 5. Narrate the concrete transformation that occurs upon adopting the solution → 3-4 lines with measurable result if it exists. 6. Paint the "new reality" of the transformed customer → 2-3 evocative lines. 7. Close with social proof or invitation → 1-2 CTA lines. 8. Condense into a short version of 100-150 words → summary. OUTPUT: Document with "Long version (complete narrative)" and "Short version (for bio, profile, or pitch introduction)"; evocative and concrete language; no corporate jargon. EDGE CASES: (a) Single-founder brand → the founder may have their own journey woven into the customer's, clearly differentiating both roles; (b) Technical or abstract product → use a everyday metaphor for the elixir/transformation; (c) Multiple customer segments → build one version per segment and note it. [C · CRITERIA] The customer is the unambiguous hero (the brand never positions itself as protagonist). The transformation is concrete and verifiable. The short version can be read in 30 seconds. Trade-off: emotion > technical product accuracy. DoD: two versions written, reviewed, and ready to insert into communication materials. Protocolo MetodologIA: declare as [SUPUESTO] any characteristic of the ideal customer that was not explicitly provided.
spec-comunicacion_story_caso_exito: [S · SITUATION] A company or professional has one or more successful projects or clients and needs to document them as persuasive success stories that serve as a commercial tool. Current success stories are flat descriptions with no narrative structure or emotional impact. [P · REQUEST] A complete success story structured in the Challenge → Action → Result sequence, ready to publish on a website, commercial proposal, or sales presentation, including: (1) magnetic headline, (2) 3-line executive summary, (3) narrative development in 3 sections, (4) customer quote, (5) result metrics in visual-text format, and (6) next-step CTA. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: B2B content consultant specialized in writing case studies and consultative sales materials. ASSUMPTIONS: the case describes a real or representative client; if there is no customer name, use "Client in the [X] sector"; metrics without an exact figure are presented as ranges or relative percentages marked [SUPUESTO]; development length is 400-600 words; if confidence in the customer's data is below 0.85, request validation before publishing. INPUTS: project notes, customer conversation, result email, or any evidence pasted into the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the client's central challenge (situation before, pain, constraints) → 1 paragraph. 2. Describe the concrete actions taken (methodology, tools, team) → 1-2 paragraphs. 3. Quantify and narrate the result obtained (metrics + transformation) → 1 paragraph + metrics table. 4. Write a magnetic headline of fewer than 10 words → 3 options. 5. Write a 3-line executive summary → draft. 6. Select or paraphrase a customer quote → 1-2 sentences. 7. Write a next-step CTA → 1 sentence. 8. Assemble the complete case → final artifact. OUTPUT: Document "Success story: [Title]" with all sections in order; narrative and results-oriented tone; without unnecessary technical jargon. EDGE CASES: (a) Customer does not authorize use of name/logo → anonymize with sector and company size; (b) No quantifiable metrics → build a qualitative impact scale (before/after on a descriptive scale) and note it; (c) Partially failed project → omit the case or restructure as "lessons learned" only if the customer approves. [C · CRITERIA] The challenge resonates emotionally with the target prospect. The metrics are specific or clearly marked as estimated. The complete case is read in fewer than 2 minutes. Trade-off: persuasive narrative > exhaustive technical report. DoD: complete success story, with headline, summary, development, quote, metrics, and CTA, ready to publish. Protocolo MetodologIA: label as [DATO REAL] or [SUPUESTO] each figure included.
spec-comunicacion_story_origen_fundador: [S · SITUATION] A founder, entrepreneur, or independent professional needs to build their origin story to communicate authentically why they created their company or project. The story will serve for the about page, investor pitch, conferences, or public profiles, and must connect emotionally with the target audience while establishing credibility. [P · REQUEST] A founder origin story in three versions: (1) complete narrative version of 300-400 words, (2) condensed version of 60-80 words for a bio or presentation, and (3) 3-phrase version for a social profile header or card. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Brand biographer and executive communication coach specialized in founder stories for pitch contexts, digital content, and public relations. ASSUMPTIONS: the story must have a turning-point or revelation moment that explains the "why"; if no personal data is provided, it is built with scaffolding questions the user must answer; the tone is authentic and vulnerable-professional, never hagiographic; if confidence in the narrative's coherence is below 0.85, flag inconsistencies before drafting. INPUTS: biographical notes, answers to scaffolding questions, or any prior founder material pasted into the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the founder's "world before" (context, career, prior beliefs) → 2-line synthesis. 2. Locate the "hinge moment" or problem that triggered the founding decision → 1 paragraph. 3. Articulate the vision or conviction that emerged from that moment → 2-3 sentences. 4. Connect that vision to the impact the company generates today → 1 paragraph. 5. Draft the complete narrative version assembling the 4 parts → 300-400 words. 6. Condense into a 60-80 word bio version → synthesis. 7. Distill into 3 phrases for a social profile → micro-version. OUTPUT: Document with three titled versions, usage notes for each, and suggestions for where to publish. EDGE CASES: (a) Founder without a clear "dramatic moment" → build around an accumulation of observations or gradual frustration, avoiding artificiality; (b) Sensitive personal story (illness, financial breakdown) → handle with emotional care and ask the founder for their desired level of openness; (c) Co-founders → build a shared origin story with a singular voice or an alternative per founder. [C · CRITERIA] The story clearly answers "why this and why you?" The short version does not lose the hinge moment. The tone is authentic, not generic-corporate. Trade-off: authentic vulnerability > perfect image. DoD: three versions drafted, reviewed, and ready to publish with usage notes. Protocolo MetodologIA: distinguish between facts provided by the founder [HECHO] and narrative elements inferred or constructed [NARRATIVA].
spec-comunicacion_story_anecdota_apertur: [S · SITUATION] A speaker, facilitator, or professional needs to open a talk, conference, or training session with a personal anecdote that captures the audience's attention in the first 90 seconds, establishes the topic's relevance, and generates emotional connection. The anecdote must function as a hook that leads to the central point of the presentation. [P · REQUEST] A structured opening anecdote ready to rehearse and present, of 200-280 words, that includes: (1) a specific scenario with sensory details, (2) tension or an unexpected twist, (3) resolution or revelation, and (4) a 2-line bridge that connects the anecdote to the talk's topic. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Executive presentation coach and speechwriter with experience in TED conferences, corporate keynotes, and training programs. ASSUMPTIONS: the anecdote is first-person (the speaker); if there is no biographical material, it is built with a representative situation marked [CONSTRUIDA — validate with speaker]; the tone is conversational-authentic, not literary; sensory details (sight, sound, physical context) make the scene concrete; if confidence in the talk's topic is below 0.85, ask for the central message before drafting. INPUTS: talk topic, central point to communicate, and any raw anecdote or biographical note pasted into the thread. STEPS: 1. Identify the central message of the talk → 1 sentence. 2. Extract or construct a specific situation that contrasts or illustrates that message → scene draft. 3. Add concrete sensory details (place, moment, sensation) → enriched version. 4. Insert the tension or unexpected twist → narrative turning point. 5. Draft the resolution or revelation → 2-3 lines. 6. Write the bridge to the talk's topic → 2 transition lines. 7. Assemble the complete anecdote → 200-280 word artifact. OUTPUT: Opening anecdote text with rehearsal title, delivery notes (where to pause, emphasis) in brackets in the margin, and the final bridge highlighted. EDGE CASES: (a) Speaker without relevant personal anecdotes → build with a close third-party situation (colleague, client) with a change of voice and authenticity warning; (b) Very technical audience → calibrate the level of emotional detail to avoid seeming out of context; (c) Opening time under 2 minutes → compress to a 120-word flash version with structure: scene-tension-revelation-bridge. [C · CRITERIA] The complete anecdote fits within 90 seconds of reading aloud. The bridge connects without forcing the central message. The listener can visualize the scene.
