spec-ia-automatizacion_integracion-embed:
[S · SITUATION] You need to build or improve a semantic search or RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system that requires converting text documents into embedding vectors and storing them in a queryable vector store. The challenge is to correctly handle the embeddings model versioning, the chunking of long documents, the incremental update of the index, and the traceability of which embedding version was used for each vector. [P · REQUEST] Design and implement a versioned embeddings pipeline that covers: document ingestion, strategic chunking, embedding generation with version metadata, storage in a vector store, and incremental update without re-processing already embedded documents. [E · EXECUTION] ROLE: Senior AI data engineer specialized in RAG architectures, embeddings pipelines, and vector stores. ASSUMPTIONS: if the embeddings model is not specified, use text-embedding-3-small from OpenAI or voyage-3 from Voyage AI; if the vector store is not indicated, use ChromaDB or pgvector depending on whether the stack is standalone or already has PostgreSQL; default chunk size 512 tokens with 50 tokens of overlap. Ask only if the document type and update frequency are unclear. INPUTS: description of the documents to be embedded (type, typical length, update frequency) and the available vector store. STEPS: 1. Design the metadata schema: document_id, chunk_index, embedding_model, embedding_version, created_at, content_hash. 2. Implement the chunker with a semantic strategy (by paragraph or section) and configurable overlap. 3. Implement the embedding function with batch processing and rate limit handling. 4. Implement the incremental update logic using content_hash to detect changes. 5. Add the migration mechanism for when the embeddings model is changed: re-embed only the affected documents. OUTPUT: (a) Pipeline architecture diagram in Mermaid; (b) complete Python module with chunker, embedder, and upserter; (c) metadata schema for the vector store; (d) migration script for an embeddings model change; (e) sample semantic search query. EDGE CASES: (1) The document changes but the affected chunk is only one out of twenty — solution: use content_hash per individual chunk, not per complete document. (2) The embeddings model is discontinued — solution: keep the embedding_model field in the metadata and run the migration script in batches. (3) The vector store reaches its storage limit — solution: implement a TTL policy for chunks of archived documents. [C · CRITERIA] The pipeline must be idempotent: running it twice on the same documents must not create duplicates. The incremental update must process only the modified chunks. The metadata schema must allow filtering by embedding version. Trade-off: chunk size vs. retrieval precision — document the choice and provide a calibration guide. DoD: executable pipeline, idempotency verified with a double-run test, and embeddings migration demonstrated.

MetodologIA Protocol: run the pipeline twice on the same set of documents and confirm there are no duplicates before closing.
spec-ia-automatizacion_integracion-obser:
[S · SITUATION] An engineering team operating systems with language model calls in production needs to instrument complete observability to detect quality degradations, optimize costs, diagnose failures, and comply with audits, without interrupting the inference flow.

[P · REQUEST] Produce: (1) a taxonomy of LLM observability metrics classified by dimension (latency, quality, cost, errors, usage); (2) a trace (span) schema for each LLM call with mandatory and optional fields; (3) the specification of critical alerts with threshold, severity, and response action; (4) an observability dashboard described with panels, metrics, and charts; (5) an implementation guide with sample code to instrument the LLM call with the specified stack.

[E · EXECUTION]
ROLE: Senior platform engineer specialized in AI systems observability, with experience in OpenTelemetry, Langfuse, Datadog, and LLM monitoring platforms.

ASSUMPTIONS: The default observability stack is OpenTelemetry + Langfuse; if another stack is specified (Datadog, Prometheus, MLflow) it is adapted; the LLM calls are to the Anthropic Claude API unless indicated; the instrumentation language is Python unless indicated; cost metrics are based on input/output tokens with a reference price marked as [ASSUMPTION].

INPUTS: Paste the current LLM call code or describe the system in the conversation thread.

STEPS:
1. Define the metrics taxonomy: ≥15 metrics classified by dimension with unit of measurement and capture frequency.
2. Design the trace schema: field, type, mandatory/optional, description, and example value for each field.
3. Specify ≥8 critical alerts: metric, threshold, severity (P1/P2/P3), trigger condition, and response action.
4. Describe the dashboard: ≥6 panels with title, chart type, included metrics, and visualization period.
5. Write the implementation guide: dependency installation, commented instrumentation code, exporter configuration, and verification.

OUTPUT: Markdown document with: metrics taxonomy table, trace schema table, critical alerts table, dashboard panel descriptions, and an implementation code block with explanatory comments.

EDGE CASES:
- LLM call with streaming → capture first-token metrics (TTFT) and time between additional tokens; do not calculate total latency until the last chunk.
- High call frequency (>100 req/s) → implement adaptive sampling for traces; always capture metrics.
- Call that fails silently (empty or truncated response) → include an empty-response rate metric and a specific alert.

[C · CRITERIA] The taxonomy covers the 5 dimensions with ≥3 metrics per dimension; the trace schema has all the fields necessary to reconstruct a complete call for audit; the alerts have quantified thresholds and concrete response actions; the implementation code is executable without modifications on the defined stack. Trade-off: observability granularity vs. performance overhead — always capture metrics, sample traces. DoD: complete taxonomy, trace schema with no ambiguous fields, ≥8 alerts with thresholds, and functional implementation code.

MetodologIA Protocol: Instrument LLM observability with actionable metrics, auditable traces, and alerts with quantified thresholds.
